issues.title: 925 obstacles between you and everywhere
issues.category_name: Movement, checkpoints and the permit regime
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: Movement inside the West Bank is not a road network with some checkpoints on it. It is an obstacle regime that OCHA counts, item by item, and the count has been rising for three years.

details.aspect: The count, and its composition
details.description: As of December 2025 OCHA documented 925 movement obstacles restricting 3.4 million Palestinians: 89 checkpoints staffed 24/7, 218 partial checkpoints, 232 road gates, 114 linear closures such as earthwalls and trenches, 167 earthmounds and 105 roadblocks.
details.energy_note: Nine hundred and twenty-five separate reasons to be late.
details.source_name: OCHA, Movement and Access in the West Bank

details.aspect: It is 43% above the twenty-year average
details.description: The 20-year annual average is 647 obstacles. The current figure is 43% higher, and about half of the increase since early 2023 was already in place by March 2024.
details.energy_note: Not a bad year. A different regime.

details.aspect: The infrastructure became permanent, which is the real change
details.description: Checkpoints and road gates are now nearly 60% of all obstacles. Two decades ago that elaborate infrastructure was 15%, and roughly 73% of obstacles were ad hoc earthmounds and roadblocks. Temporary inconvenience has been rebuilt in concrete and steel.
details.energy_note: They stopped pretending it was temporary.

details.aspect: Gates are the growth product
details.description: Over 120 new road gates were installed in 2025. Gates rose from 34% of all obstacles in February 2025 (288 of 849) to more than 41% by December (384 of 925). A gate costs nothing to close and needs no soldier standing at it.
details.energy_note: A padlock is cheaper than a checkpoint and works better.

details.aspect: What they actually cut off
details.description: At least 459 obstacles - half of them - block or hinder access between Palestinian villages and the main roads. At least 20% block access to agricultural land, about 60% of those being earthmounds and roadblocks.
details.energy_note: Your village, and the road, and a pile of earth between them.

details.aspect: The journey has no timetable, which is the cost
details.description: A 25km trip can take 40 minutes or five hours and there is no way to know which before setting out. Every appointment must be planned for the worst case, so the buffer time is spent whether or not the delay happens.
details.time_note: Cumulative days per year lost to buffer and delay.
details.energy_note: Paying for the traffic jam that didn't happen.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the 09:00 appointment
details.description: The clinic in Ramallah opens at nine. She leaves Nablus at half five because of Za'tara, sits ninety minutes at a gate that turns out to be open, arrives at 07:40 and waits on a plastic chair for eighty minutes. The appointment lasts eleven minutes.
details.energy_note: Four hours of travel for eleven minutes of medicine.

details.aspect: Two things OCHA does not count
details.description: The count excludes checkpoints on the Green Line and excludes 'closed military zone' declarations and the closure of Jenin and Tulkarm camps for returnees. The real number of things that can stop you is higher than the number in the report.
details.energy_note: Even the count of the obstacles is an undercount.

details.aspect: You stop planning anything that requires crossing
details.description: The rational adaptation is to shrink your life to what is reachable without a checkpoint: the job in town rather than the better one in the city, the local college rather than the good one, the cousin you see rather than the aunt you don't. Nobody records this as a restriction because nobody applied for anything.
details.energy_note: A life sized to fit between two checkpoints.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the December 2025 composition, item by item
details.description: 925 obstacles restricting 3.4 million people: 89 checkpoints staffed 24/7, 218 partial checkpoints, 232 road gates, 114 linear closures such as earthwalls and trenches, 167 earthmounds and 105 roadblocks. Against a twenty-year annual average of 647.
details.energy_note: Counted, itemised, and 43% above the twenty-year average.

issues.title: Applying for permission to move inside your own territory
issues.category_name: Movement, checkpoints and the permit regime
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: The permit is the master mechanism. It is discretionary, time-limited, purpose-bound, secret in its criteria, and can be refused by silence rather than by refusal.

details.aspect: The eligibility criteria exclude most people before they apply
details.description: Gaza residents may apply to visit first-degree relatives only if those relatives are dying, have died, or are getting married. Gisha's point is that the criteria are built so that the vast majority are never even considered.
details.energy_note: You may see your sister if she is dying. Not if she is ill.

details.aspect: Denial by silence is the commonest denial
details.description: Authorities routinely do not answer, or answer after the travel date has passed. Gisha calls non-response the most troubling form of bureaucratic violence, because there is nothing to appeal against.
details.energy_note: Not refused. Just never answered.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - one month of non-response, from one organisation's caseload
details.description: A woman could not visit a terminally ill sister. A man needing eye treatment in Jerusalem rescheduled six times. A couple postponed fertility treatment. A man was stranded in Gaza ten months, unable to return home. A young woman awaiting urgent cancer treatment filed six separate requests. All of them met Israel's own narrow criteria.
details.energy_note: Six applications for one course of cancer treatment.

details.aspect: The 'security block' rests on material you cannot see
details.description: Thousands are placed under security blocks that turn out to be arbitrary. The material is confidential and is withheld from the applicant and from her lawyer, so the case cannot be argued, only petitioned against.
details.energy_note: Accused of nothing, in a document you may not read.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the physician denied twice, cleared twice on the courthouse steps
details.description: A Gaza doctor applied in 2018 to reach Ramallah for Palestinian Medical Council certification exams. Denied on unspecified security grounds. Gisha petitioned the High Court; the ban was retracted before the hearing and the state was ordered to pay 3,000 ILS costs. February 2019, second set of exams, denied again on unspecified security grounds. The state withdrew immediately after the second petition was filed.
details.money_note: 3,000 ILS costs awarded against the state.
details.energy_note: A security threat twice, and not once the state would defend in court.
details.notes: The mechanism: a block that evaporates the moment it must be justified.

details.aspect: Punishment by relative
details.description: In seven petitions for Palestinian Christians denied permits to reach holy sites and family, the ground cited in all seven was 'overstay' - meaning a relative of theirs had at some point overstayed a permit. Gisha argues this is arbitrary collective punishment; it is also routine.
details.energy_note: Refused for something your cousin did in 2014.

details.aspect: The desperation is itself a lever
details.description: Gisha reports authorities exploiting applicants' need in order to extract information about neighbours or relatives. The permit queue doubles as a recruitment queue.
details.energy_note: The price of the permit is a name.

details.aspect: From January 2022 even the lawyers were cut out
details.description: The Gaza CLA refused to answer inquiries from human rights organisations and lawyers acting for Gaza residents - despite legal intervention often being the only route by which a permit is ever obtained.
details.energy_note: They closed the one door that sometimes opened.

issues.title: The flying checkpoint: an obstacle with no location
issues.category_name: Movement, checkpoints and the permit regime
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: A staffed checkpoint can at least be routed around. A flying checkpoint is erected without notice on any road at any hour, which means no route is ever reliable and no journey can be planned.

details.aspect: Unpredictability is the mechanism, not a side effect
details.description: The value of a flying checkpoint is precisely that you cannot know where it will be. It converts the whole road network into a probabilistic system.
details.energy_note: Every road, potentially, today.

details.aspect: It lands hardest on anything with a fixed time
details.description: Dialysis, chemotherapy, an exam, a shift, a wedding, a court date, labour. Anything that cannot be rescheduled is the thing most exposed.
details.energy_note: The appointments you cannot move are the ones it hits.

details.aspect: Soldiers are the whole procedure
details.description: There is no published standard, no service time, no complaint route and no name. Two 19-year-olds decide how long several hundred people wait.
details.energy_note: An unappealable decision made by a teenager.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the interview
details.description: She has a job interview in Ramallah at eleven. At 09:20 a jeep parks across the road outside Sinjil. At 11:40 she calls to explain and is told, politely, that they have already seen the other candidates.
details.money_note: A year of the salary not earned.
details.energy_note: Losing a job to a parked vehicle.

details.aspect: Employers learn to price it in, and stop hiring
details.description: An employer who needs reliable attendance eventually prefers the applicant who does not cross a checkpoint to get to work. The restriction becomes a hiring criterion that nobody ever states.
details.energy_note: Unemployable because of where you sleep.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the gate that is counted but not staffed
details.description: OCHA's December 2025 breakdown lists 232 road gates, 159 of them frequently closed, and 218 partial checkpoints of which 152 have gates - 90 usually open, 62 frequently closed. A gate needs no soldier, so closure costs the army nothing and cannot be anticipated by the driver.
details.energy_note: Three hundred and eighty-four gates, and no timetable for any of them.

issues.title: The colour of your number plate decides which roads exist
issues.category_name: Movement, checkpoints and the permit regime
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: The road regime runs on vehicle registration, not on identity documents. A Palestinian-plated car is barred from roads that an Israeli-plated car uses freely, and the rule has never been written down.

details.aspect: It exists nowhere in writing
details.description: B'Tselem found the forbidden roads regime has never been set out in Knesset legislation, political decisions, military orders, press releases or even road signs. It runs on verbal orders to soldiers and on practice.
details.energy_note: A law you can be punished under and never read.

details.aspect: Three tiers of prohibition
details.description: Completely prohibited roads, for Israeli vehicles only, including what the army calls 'sterile roads' with a checkpoint that passes Israeli vehicles only; partially prohibited roads needing a Civil Administration permit; and restricted-use roads, nominally open but blocked with concrete.
details.energy_note: Open, permitted, or blocked with a concrete cube.

details.aspect: Roughly 105km barred outright by plate colour
details.description: B'Tselem found Palestinian-plated vehicles completely barred from about 105km of West Bank roads. The driver's documents are irrelevant; the plate decides.
details.energy_note: Your car is the wrong nationality.

details.aspect: The planning vocabulary says it plainly
details.description: Israeli planning distinguishes 'fabric of life' roads, which divert Palestinian traffic away from settlers, from 'bypass' roads, which divert settlers away from Palestinian towns. Both exist to keep the two apart; only one is built to a good standard.
details.energy_note: Two road networks, one country, one of them resurfaced.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - Route 4370
details.description: A road near Jerusalem with a concrete wall down the middle: one side for Israeli vehicles, the other for Palestinian traffic. It became the emblem because it makes the arrangement literally visible.
details.energy_note: A wall down the centre line of a road.

details.aspect: Being forced onto back roads has a compounding cost
details.description: Poorly maintained secondary routes mean longer journeys, more fuel, more vehicle wear, more accidents and more exposure to the villages where settler violence happens.
details.money_note: Annual fuel, wear and repair premium.
details.energy_note: A worse road, and more of it.

details.aspect: It fragments the territory, which is the point
details.description: The network is arranged so that Palestinian areas connect to each other badly and settlements connect to Israel well. The daily cost is time; the structural effect is that the places do not join up.
details.energy_note: A map designed so the pieces don't touch.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - Route 443, and the one time a court intervened
details.description: In 2009 Israel's Supreme Court issued a first-of-its-kind ruling ordering the army to reopen a West Bank highway to Palestinian traffic. It concerned Route 443, where obstacles on both sides prevented Palestinians from driving to and from nearby villages. One road, one ruling, in two decades of the regime.
details.energy_note: One highway, reopened by a court, once.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - October 2005, the temporary measure that stayed
details.description: Israel barred private Palestinian vehicles from several West Bank highways in October 2005, expanding a network of settler-only routes after a drive-by shooting killed three settlers. The army billed the restrictions as temporary security measures; a plan was then considered to permanently designate roads for separate use.
details.energy_note: Announced as temporary in 2005, still in force.

issues.title: Area C: 60% of the West Bank you may cross but not use
issues.category_name: Movement, checkpoints and the permit regime
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: The Oslo division was meant to be transitional. Three decades on it is the planning regime, and the largest of the three areas is the one where Palestinian building, farming and infrastructure are effectively prohibited.

details.aspect: The proportions
details.description: Area C is over 60% of the West Bank and is under full Israeli civil and security control. Palestinians may build in less than 1% of it.
details.energy_note: Sixty per cent of the land, one per cent of it available.

details.aspect: It is where the utilities have to go
details.description: Water mains, power lines, telecom masts, roads and sewage all have to cross Area C to connect anything to anything. Refusing permits there constrains development in Areas A and B without touching them.
details.energy_note: Control the middle and you control both ends.

details.aspect: Telecom masts specifically
details.description: Palestinian operators cannot readily erect towers in Area C, which is why coverage and capacity are poor in areas nominally under Palestinian control.
details.energy_note: Your bad signal is a planning decision.
details.notes: See TEC-001 for the spectrum side of the same problem.

details.aspect: The land is still yours on paper
details.description: Ownership is not extinguished; use is. A family can hold a deed to land it may not build on, plant on, fence, or reach without coordination.
details.energy_note: Owning a field you are not allowed to walk into.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the mast that cannot be built
details.description: Palestinian operators cannot readily erect telecom towers in Area C, which is over 60% of the West Bank and sits between every Palestinian population centre. The result is poor coverage inside Areas A and B, which are nominally under Palestinian control - a planning refusal in one area degrading a service in another.
details.energy_note: Bad signal in your own city, decided in a planning office.

issues.title: There is no airport, and the one nearby is closed to you
issues.category_name: Borders, crossings and the airport you are not allowed to use
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Gaza's airport was destroyed in 2002. Ben Gurion is an hour from Ramallah and West Bank Palestinians are barred from using it. The only way out is through Jordan.

details.aspect: The rule
details.description: Most West Bank Palestinians are barred from travelling abroad through Ben Gurion. Holders of a Palestinian passport and green ID may cross from Jordan only via the King Hussein Bridge - not at other crossings, not through the airport.
details.energy_note: The airport is forty minutes away and it is not for you.

details.aspect: So every flight starts with an international border
details.description: Queen Alia in Amman becomes the home airport. Reaching it means the Jericho side, the Israeli side at Allenby, the Jordanian side at King Hussein, then a drive to Amman - before check-in.
details.money_note: Crossing fees, transit, taxis, per trip, each way.
details.energy_note: Three borders before the departures board.

details.aspect: The hotel you must buy because of opening hours
details.description: For about two decades Allenby ran 08:00-23:30 on weekdays and 08:00-15:30 at weekends. An early flight from Amman therefore required crossing the day before and paying for a night, or sleeping in the terminal.
details.money_note: A night in Amman, per trip, forced by the timetable.
details.energy_note: A hotel bill created by a gate's closing time.

details.aspect: It took over a decade of US pressure to extend the hours
details.description: American administrations pushed for more than ten years. Israel moved Allenby to near-full-time operation in 2023, after an earlier 24/7 pilot lasting one week was reversed.
details.energy_note: Ten years of diplomacy to open a gate at night.

details.aspect: A cheap flight is not cheap
details.description: The headline fare is the smallest component. Crossing fees, two taxis, a hotel, a day of leave each way and the risk of the whole thing being cancelled at the bridge are the actual price.
details.money_note: Per journey, on top of the ticket.
details.energy_note: The ticket is the cheap part.

details.aspect: Which prices you out of the things that need travel
details.description: A conference, a job interview, a scholarship weekend, a funeral. Each costs two days and several hundred dollars more for you than for the other person invited, so you decline more of them, and the pattern of declining becomes your career.
details.energy_note: Saying no to things because of a bridge.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the one-week experiment
details.description: An earlier 24/7 arrangement at Allenby, requested by the Biden administration, ran as a pilot for one week and was then reversed. Israel moved to near-full-time operation only in 2023, after more than a decade of US pressure.
details.energy_note: A week of normal opening hours, then back.

issues.title: Allenby: the single gateway, and what happens when it shuts
issues.category_name: Borders, crossings and the airport you are not allowed to use
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: One crossing carries the entire outbound movement of the West Bank. A single point of failure is not a design flaw here; it is the design.

details.aspect: Three sides, three queues, three sets of rules
details.description: The Palestinian side at Jericho, the Israeli side at Allenby, the Jordanian side at King Hussein. Each has its own procedures and its own capacity to stop you, and clearing one says nothing about the next.
details.energy_note: Cleared three times, refused once, and that's the trip.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - September 2025, closed indefinitely with no notice
details.description: Israel abruptly closed the crossing, stranding Palestinians abroad, forcing patients being treated in Jordan to extend their stays, and separating families. It announced reopening to foot traffic only the following day.
details.money_note: Extended hotel and treatment costs while stranded.
details.energy_note: Locked out of your own country on a Wednesday.

details.aspect: Being stranded abroad is the expensive direction
details.description: When it closes while you are outside, the costs run: accommodation, missed work, rebooked flights, a visa in the transit country that may expire, and no date at which any of it ends.
details.energy_note: A closure with no end date, and you are on the wrong side.

details.aspect: You cannot insure against it
details.description: Travel insurance does not cover a border closure by the occupying power, and airlines do not treat it as a disruption they caused. The loss sits entirely with the traveller.
details.energy_note: Nobody's fault, therefore your bill.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the scan in Amman
details.description: Her mother's oncology follow-up is in Amman because the machine in Nablus has been waiting on a part for seven months. They cross on the Sunday. On the Tuesday the bridge closes. The follow-up becomes eleven days in a cousin's flat, and the appointment after it is missed entirely.
details.energy_note: A cancer schedule, kept by a border guard.

issues.title: Rafah, and the price of a place in the queue
issues.category_name: Borders, crossings and the airport you are not allowed to use
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: Gaza's crossing to Egypt has operated intermittently for two decades. When it opens, access to it is rationed - and the rationing has a price list.

details.aspect: Registration, then waiting, then maybe
details.description: Travel requires registering and waiting for a name to appear on a list published at intervals nobody controls. The waiting is measured in months.
details.energy_note: On a list, in a queue, for a gate that may not open.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - $500 to skip the line, and it still did not work
details.description: Afaf al-Najar, 19, won a scholarship to study communications in Turkey, secured every document, and paid $500 to skip the long lines at Rafah. Palestinian border officials blocked her anyway - under the guardian rule.
details.money_note: Paid to bypass the queue. Non-refundable.
details.energy_note: Bought her way to the front, and was turned back at it.
details.notes: Two separate authorities stopped the same journey. See WOM-004.

details.aspect: The informal market is the actual system
details.description: Where a queue is long, scarce and opaque, brokerage appears. The fee is not a bribe to an individual so much as the market price of a public process that does not function.
details.energy_note: A tariff for something that should be free.

details.aspect: Which means mobility is means-tested by accident
details.description: Those who can pay travel. Those who cannot, wait. Nobody designed that as policy and it is the reliable outcome of every opaque queue.
details.energy_note: A border that quietly checks your bank balance.

issues.title: Being refused entry to the place you are from
issues.category_name: Borders, crossings and the airport you are not allowed to use
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Return is not guaranteed. For a Palestinian abroad, going home is an application, and a refusal at the bridge is not appealable from outside.

details.aspect: The one-way-door problem
details.description: Leaving is easier than returning. A person who goes abroad to study or work may find the residency they left with no longer recognised on the way back.
details.energy_note: The exit is free. The return is the application.
details.notes: Directly parallel to RET-001 in assets/text/iran.

details.aspect: Refusal happens at the border, where there is no lawyer
details.description: The decision is taken at a crossing, by an official, in minutes, with no written reasons and no counsel present. Challenging it afterwards means doing so from another country.
details.money_note: Legal costs of a challenge mounted from abroad.
details.energy_note: Litigating your way home from a hotel.

details.aspect: It changes what going abroad means
details.description: Studying overseas stops being an opportunity and becomes a gamble against your own residency. Many decline scholarships for exactly this reason.
details.energy_note: A degree, against the risk of the door closing.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the PhD
details.description: Four years in Leipzig. She is careful: she visits every eighteen months, keeps utility bills, keeps the flat in her mother's name. At the bridge in the fifth year, a man in his twenties looks at a screen and says the centre of her life appears to be in Germany.
details.money_note: The value of a residency lost.
details.energy_note: A doctorate, traded for a city.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the returnee camps excluded from the count
details.description: OCHA's obstacle count explicitly excludes the closure of Jenin and Tulkarm refugee camps for returnees - meaning people barred from re-entering their own camp do not appear in the headline figure for movement restrictions at all.
details.energy_note: Barred from your own camp, and not counted as restricted.

issues.title: Israel holds the registry that says you exist
issues.category_name: The population registry, the colour of your ID, and residency
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: The Palestinian population registry is controlled by Israel. Births, marriages, divorces, deaths and address changes all require Israeli approval before the Palestinian Authority may issue or amend an ID.

details.aspect: Every life event is an application
details.description: A birth is not a fact to be recorded but a request to be approved. The PA may amend or issue an ID card only after Israeli approval, and Israel updates its own copy, which is the one that governs permits.
details.energy_note: Your daughter is born, and then applied for.

details.aspect: This is more than Oslo provided for
details.description: Under the accords, a holder of an Israeli-approved ID may reside anywhere in the Palestinian territory, with Israel's authority limited to controlling entry into Israel and passage between the two areas. The registry control exceeds that.
details.energy_note: A power that outgrew the agreement it came from.

details.aspect: An unregistered child is an administrative non-person
details.description: Without registry entry there is no ID, and without an ID there is no school enrolment, no health insurance, no travel document, no permit application and no legal identity.
details.energy_note: A child who exists everywhere except on the system.

details.aspect: The children of smuggled sperm are a documented case of exactly this
details.description: Israel has denied identification documents or legal status to babies conceived from sperm smuggled out of prisons, and those children are denied visits to their imprisoned fathers.
details.energy_note: Born, and refused a number.
details.notes: See DET-004 for the practice itself. Over 60 such babies by 2018.

details.aspect: It means the occupation is administrative before it is military
details.description: Most days there is no soldier. There is a clerk, a database and a form, and they decide more about the shape of the year than the soldier does.
details.energy_note: Ruled by a spreadsheet you have no login for.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - Bidoon: the people with no number
details.description: Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank cannot obtain PA travel documents without an Israeli-issued national number, which requires a record in the Israeli civil registry. Those without one are called Bidoon - literally 'without'. The category exists and has a name.
details.energy_note: There is a word for people the registry never recorded.

issues.title: Green ID, blue ID, and what each one forbids
issues.category_name: The population registry, the colour of your ID, and residency
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Which document you hold is mostly an accident of where a relative was standing in 1967. It determines which roads, cities, hospitals and countries are available to you for the rest of your life.

details.aspect: The tiers
details.description: West Bank green ID, Gaza ID, East Jerusalem blue permanent residency, and Israeli citizenship for '48 Palestinians. Four documents, four different sets of permitted movements, one people.
details.energy_note: Your rights arrive in a colour.

details.aspect: It decides who you can marry without consequence
details.description: Marrying across the tiers is the commonest way a family ends up living in two places, because the registry will not merge the two statuses.
details.energy_note: Falling in love with the wrong document.
details.notes: See FAM-001 and FAM-002.

details.aspect: And which hospital you may reach
details.description: The specialist centres are largely in East Jerusalem. A green ID cannot reach them without a permit, which means the referral and the permit are two separate processes with two separate failure modes.
details.energy_note: Referred to a hospital you are not allowed to enter.
details.notes: See MED-001.

details.aspect: Nobody chose their tier and everybody is judged by it
details.description: Within Palestinian society the tiers carry status, suspicion and resentment - the Jerusalemite with the blue card, the Gazan who cannot leave. The hierarchy is externally imposed and internally felt.
details.energy_note: Sorted into ranks by a filing system.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - 340,000 people holding the document that is not a passport
details.description: Roughly 340,000 East Jerusalem Palestinians hold the Israeli laissez-passer, about 75% of all its holders. Most also hold Jordanian passports, but mostly temporary foreigner's passports rather than nationality passports. Residents were offered Israeli citizenship after the 1967 annexation and most declined for political reasons.
details.energy_note: Three hundred and forty thousand, sorted into a tier by one decision in 1967.

issues.title: Jerusalem residency as a privilege that can be withdrawn
issues.category_name: The population registry, the colour of your ID, and residency
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: East Jerusalem Palestinians were made permanent residents, not citizens. Permanent residency is revocable, and the criteria for revoking it were widened after the fact.

details.aspect: The status itself
details.description: Annexation classified Palestinians in the city as permanent residents. Rights groups describe this as converting an inherent right to live in and enter Jerusalem into a revocable privilege.
details.energy_note: A birthright, reissued as a licence.

details.aspect: The rules were changed underneath people
details.description: Originally residency survived absence of under seven years, and moving elsewhere in the West Bank did not affect it at all. From the mid-1990s the criteria were broadened: moving your 'centre of life' outside Israel - including into the rest of the occupied territory - now costs the status.
details.energy_note: The goalposts moved, retroactively, for everyone.

details.aspect: The scale
details.description: More than 14,565 Palestinian residencies were revoked between 1967 and 2015.
details.energy_note: Fourteen thousand quiet deportations.

details.aspect: Proving your centre of life is a permanent documentary chore
details.description: Utility bills, school registrations, rent contracts, municipal tax, employer letters - assembled continuously, for years, against the possibility of being asked. The burden of proof sits on the resident.
details.time_note: Days per year spent maintaining the evidence file.
details.energy_note: Filing paperwork to prove you live in your own house.

details.aspect: A second ground was added in 2006: breach of allegiance
details.description: Since 2006 the Interior Minister has also revoked residency punitively for 'breach of allegiance', which reaches even people who never left the city at all.
details.energy_note: You can lose it without ever going anywhere.

details.aspect: It interlocks with the family unification freeze
details.description: A family awaiting unification must choose: live apart, or have the Jerusalem spouse move out to join the other - which triggers loss of the Jerusalem status under centre-of-life. Leaving also risks the PA refusing them status in the territories.
details.energy_note: Two policies that catch you between them.

details.aspect: Rights groups call it forcible transfer
details.description: HRW argues the revocations effectively force out a population protected under the Fourth Geneva Convention, which permits transfer only temporarily and for imperative military reasons.
details.energy_note: Depopulation, conducted by letter.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the 2006 ground that reaches people who never left
details.description: Since 2006, in addition to centre-of-life, the Interior Minister has revoked residency punitively for 'breach of allegiance'. This reaches Palestinians who never left Jerusalem at all, so even perfect compliance with the centre-of-life rule is not protective.
details.energy_note: Doing everything right, and still losing it.

issues.title: Registered in Gaza, living in the West Bank: illegal at home
issues.category_name: The population registry, the colour of your ID, and residency
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: Since 2000 Israel has refused to let Gaza-registered Palestinians change their ID address to the West Bank. People born and raised in the West Bank are classified as illegal aliens in it.

details.aspect: The freeze
details.description: Since 2000 Israel has refused address changes from Gaza to the West Bank even for people who have lived there for many years, and the freeze also ended the family reunification procedure that was the only lawful route.
details.energy_note: Twenty-six years of the wrong address.

details.aspect: The exception that proves it
details.description: In 2011 Israel agreed to let 5,000 West Bank-resident Palestinians with registered Gaza addresses change them. About 2,700 were approved. Against a population in that position numbering many times more.
details.energy_note: A one-off amnesty, for a fraction.

details.aspect: The procedure exists and is built to refuse
details.description: A 'Procedure for handling applications by Gaza Strip residents for settlement in the Judea and Samaria Area' has existed since 2009. A Freedom of Information response revealed it is designed for rejecting applications rather than accepting them. Gisha titled its report on it 'A procedure so special it applies to no one'.
details.energy_note: A form whose purpose is to be refused.

details.aspect: The consequence is removal to Gaza
details.description: Israel has arrested Palestinians whose registered address is Gaza - including people whose home, family and job are in the West Bank - and removed them to Gaza against their will, in some cases where the only suspected wrongdoing was being present.
details.energy_note: Deported from your own house to a place you've never lived.

details.aspect: And most of the people it is used against are women
details.description: Gisha found the procedure is being used to forcibly transfer protected persons within the occupied territory, and that most of the victims are women - typically women who married into the other area.
details.energy_note: A separation policy that mostly separates wives.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the form she was made to sign
details.description: Women who had already signed a settlement form when entering Gaza had it used against them to refuse their return to the West Bank. Women who had not signed were pressured into signing as a condition of travelling at all - whether to visit relatives or to return to their own homes.
details.energy_note: Signing away your address to be allowed through a gate.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the impossible choice, as posed at a crossing
details.description: She is told she may return to the West Bank as her ID says, or sign a form changing her address to Gaza. Her home, husband and job are in Nablus. Her son is in Gaza. The official waits while she decides which of the two to stop seeing.
details.energy_note: Choose a child or a house. Now, at this window.
details.notes: Constructed, but this is precisely the bind Gisha documents under the title 'Give up your right to live in the West Bank, or never see your children in Gaza again'.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the 2011 quota, and the arithmetic of it
details.description: Israel agreed in 2011 to allow 5,000 West Bank-resident Palestinians with registered Gaza addresses to change them; about 2,700 were approved. It was framed as a goodwill measure and functioned as confirmation that the freeze otherwise held.
details.energy_note: Two thousand seven hundred, out of a problem many times larger.

issues.title: A passport that is a travel document, not a nationality
issues.category_name: Status, statelessness and a passport that is not a nationality
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: The Palestinian Authority passport is accepted by many states as a travel document while conferring none of the things a nationality confers, because the issuing authority is not a state those countries recognise.

details.aspect: Where it ranks
details.description: As of 2026, visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 39 countries and territories, ranked 93rd by Henley. Other indices: 89th on the Global Passport Power Rank, 96th on Passport Index with a world reach of 23%, and 180th of 199 on VisaGuide's measure.
details.energy_note: Thirty-nine doors, out of roughly two hundred.

details.aspect: Accepted as a document, not as a citizenship
details.description: The United States among others accepts the passport as a valid travel document, but that acceptance does not imply recognition of citizenship, since it is not issued by a state it recognises.
details.energy_note: Good enough to travel on, not good enough to be from.

details.aspect: And three states will not take it at all
details.description: As of 2020, Georgia, Syria and Madagascar did not recognise the Palestinian passport as a valid travel document; holders had to apply using another country's refugee travel document.
details.energy_note: A passport some countries simply do not accept.
details.notes: Sourced via Chinese-language Wikipedia's 巴勒斯坦护照 entry, which carries the fullest recognition list found.

details.aspect: It does not reach the people who most need a document
details.description: Palestinians in Syria, Lebanon, Iraq and Egypt who hold no Palestinian ID card do not get one. They receive whatever special document their country of residence chooses to issue.
details.energy_note: The passport of your nation, unavailable to you.

details.aspect: Every visa application is a long-form one
details.description: A weak document means interviews rather than online forms, bank statements, sponsors, itineraries, insurance, and a refusal rate that makes the whole exercise a gamble with a non-refundable fee.
details.money_note: Per application, non-refundable.
details.energy_note: Paying to be considered, and usually refused.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the conference in Lisbon
details.description: The abstract is accepted in March for a June conference. The Portuguese appointment in Amman is in May, which requires a bridge crossing, which requires two days. The visa arrives eight days after the conference ends. She presents by video, at 2am, to an empty room.
details.energy_note: Accepted, funded, and absent.

details.aspect: The cumulative effect is a career with no international layer
details.description: Fieldwork, collaborations, fellowships, external examiners, conference networks. Each is individually blocked by an administrative delay; together they are the difference between a national and an international career.
details.money_note: Lifetime earnings and opportunity difference.
details.energy_note: A whole professional dimension, closed.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - three states that do not accept it at all
details.description: As of 2020, Georgia, Syria and Madagascar did not recognise the Palestinian passport as a valid travel document. Holders travelling there had to apply using another country's refugee travel document instead.
details.energy_note: A passport that is not a passport in three countries.

issues.title: Statelessness, inherited
issues.category_name: Status, statelessness and a passport that is not a nationality
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Refugee status passes down the generations, and most host states have deliberately not naturalised the people living in them for seventy years. The condition is heritable and the number therefore only grows.

details.aspect: Non-naturalisation is the regional norm, not an oversight
details.description: Host states have largely not permitted naturalisation, granting neither citizenship nor residency documents despite long residence: Lebanon, Syria, Egypt and the Gulf states. Jordan is the single exception, and that followed from its 1948 annexation.
details.energy_note: Seventy years resident, still a foreigner.
details.notes: Sourced via Russian-language coverage (Current Time / evolutio.info), which states the non-naturalisation rule more directly than the English sources found.

details.aspect: The status is inherited, so the population grows
details.description: Refugee status passes to descendants. Roughly 750,000 registered in 1950; over 5 million by 2013; over 5.6 million registered with UNRWA by 2019, over 1.5 million of them in the 59 recognised camps.
details.energy_note: A legal condition with a birth rate.

details.aspect: Even in Jordan, citizenship is not uniform
details.description: Jordan is the only Arab state to have granted citizenship, but not all Palestinians in Jordan hold it and not all who hold it have full rights. The presence or absence of a national number is the dividing line.
details.energy_note: A citizenship with a missing field.

details.aspect: Statelessness blocks the ordinary machinery of adult life
details.description: Property, a business licence, a professional registration, a mortgage, a pension, a marriage registration, a driving licence in some jurisdictions. Each requires a nationality field that cannot be filled.
details.energy_note: A form with a box you can never complete.

details.aspect: And it cannot be escaped by achievement
details.description: A doctorate, a business, forty years of tax and three children born in the country do not convert into status where the law does not provide for conversion. Effort is not a route out of this one.
details.energy_note: Nothing you accomplish changes the category.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - expelled from the Gulf, received by Jordan
details.description: After the 1991 Gulf War, Jordan received Palestinians expelled from Gulf states. A population holding no citizenship anywhere can be removed from anywhere, and periodically is - the expulsion requiring no legal process because there is no status to revoke.
details.energy_note: Removable from every country you have ever lived in.

issues.title: The document with no national number
issues.category_name: Status, statelessness and a passport that is not a nationality
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Jordan's ex-Gaza Palestinians hold a travel document that looks like a passport, functions as a residence permit, expires every two years, and is refused by several of the countries it would most be used for.

details.aspect: Who they are
details.description: Roughly 158,000 refugees who fled Gaza to Jordan after June 1967, per UNRWA. They were never given Jordanian citizenship and remain stateless. During Egypt's control of Gaza they had Egyptian travel documents but not Egyptian citizenship.
details.energy_note: Stateless in the country they've lived in since 1967.

details.aspect: The document itself
details.description: A temporary passport valid two years, with no national ID number. It is in effect a residency permit renewable at the state's discretion, and renewal runs through the Ministry of Interior with the prime minister's approval.
details.money_note: Renewal costs, every two years, for life.
details.energy_note: Reapplying to exist, every twenty-four months.

details.aspect: The missing number is the whole problem
details.description: Without a national number there are no political rights, no social security, and restricted job access. The document permits presence and little else.
details.energy_note: Present, and not counted.

details.aspect: Several states will not honour it
details.description: Syria, Lebanon, Egypt and some Gulf states are among those refusing to recognise the document. It is a travel document that does not reliably travel.
details.energy_note: A passport that is not accepted in the neighbouring country.

details.aspect: Late renewal makes you undocumented
details.description: Any delay in the two-year renewal risks leaving the holder with no valid status at all. An administrative backlog becomes an immigration offence.
details.energy_note: Illegal because an office was slow.

details.aspect: You may not hold both documents
details.description: Jordan does not permit stateless Palestinians to hold both a Jordanian temporary passport and a PA passport, so acquiring one may cost the other. Canada's IRB has examined whether taking a PA passport forfeits Jordanian rights entirely.
details.energy_note: Two weak documents, and you may only have one.

details.aspect: Entering Jordan requires a guarantor
details.description: Gazans are treated separately from other Palestinians in Jordan and must identify a guarantor to enter. A person without a well-placed contact does not travel.
details.energy_note: You need someone to vouch for you to go home.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the guarantor requirement
details.description: Gazans are treated separately from other Palestinians in Jordan and must identify a guarantor in order to enter. A person without a well-placed contact in the country does not travel, regardless of what their documents say.
details.energy_note: You need someone respectable to vouch for your existence.

issues.title: Naturalising abroad, and the political test attached
issues.category_name: Status, statelessness and a passport that is not a nationality
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: In some states the route out of statelessness now carries a declaration about the conflict itself, which converts a citizenship application into a test of political opinion.

details.aspect: Germany's 2024 clause
details.description: The reformed nationality law added three 'antisemitism filters', one inserted into section 10(1) sentence 1 StAG as number 1a, requiring applicants to affirm Germany's historical responsibility, peaceful coexistence of peoples, and the prohibition on the use of force in international law.
details.energy_note: A citizenship exam with a foreign policy question.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - VG Regensburg, December 2024
details.description: A stateless Palestinian, Sunni, who by his own account had never lived in Israel or Palestine but only in Syria, and was recognised as a refugee in Germany in 2016, was refused naturalisation for not recognising Israel. He argued his position was anti-Zionist rather than antisemitic. The court held that anti-Zionists cannot become Germans either - although the legislature had deliberately declined to require an explicit declaration on Israel.
details.energy_note: Refused a passport over a country he has never seen.

details.aspect: Deportation proposed without charge or conviction
details.description: The Berlin Senate sought to deport four pro-Palestinian activists over an occupation at the Free University while investigations were still running. None had been charged or convicted. Three were EU nationals and one American. Legal analysis considered the expulsions probably unlawful, not least under EU free movement.
details.energy_note: An expulsion order in advance of any charge.

details.aspect: There is precedent, and it is old
details.description: After the Black September attack at the 1972 Munich Olympics, many foreigners were expelled for membership of the General Union of Palestinian Students or Workers - association itself as the ground.
details.energy_note: Deported for belonging to a student union.

details.aspect: German-Palestinians get worse consular protection, by their own state's account
details.description: Berlin's immigration authority advises that the status derived from the Palestinian population registry is not a nationality in German law - but that Israel and the Palestinian authorities treat such Germans as dual nationals anyway, which can impede consular assistance.
details.energy_note: Your embassy may not be able to reach you.

details.aspect: Even the deportation destination is legally incoherent
details.description: The Lower Saxony higher administrative court held that naming 'Israel' as the destination state for a stateless Palestinian is defective - including with the addition 'West Bank', since the West Bank is not Israeli state territory. There is often no lawful country to deport the person to.
details.energy_note: Deportable in principle, to nowhere in particular.

details.aspect: So the safest strategy abroad is silence
details.description: Where naturalisation, residence and employment all carry a political test, the rational move is to say nothing about the place you are from, for the decade the process takes.
details.energy_note: Ten years of not mentioning where you're from.
details.notes: Connects to DIA-001 and PSY-003.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - Munich, 1972, and expulsion for membership
details.description: After the Black September attack at the 1972 Munich Olympics, West Germany expelled many foreigners for membership of the General Union of Palestinian Students or the General Union of Palestinian Workers. Association with a student body was itself the ground.
details.energy_note: Deported for being in a student union.

issues.title: The building permit that is not issued
issues.category_name: Land, home demolition and the building permit nobody gets
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: Building legally in Area C requires a permit from the Israeli Civil Administration. The approval rate is close to zero and has been for twenty-five years, which means every Palestinian home built there is unlawful by construction.

details.aspect: The approval numbers
details.description: Fewer than 4% of Palestinian applications in Area C were approved between 2015 and 2019, per the Civil Administration itself. Bimkom's data for 2016-2020: 2,550 applications, 24 approved - a rejection rate of about 99%.
details.energy_note: Twenty-four permits. Two and a half thousand families.

details.aspect: And since October 2023, zero
details.description: 282 applications submitted since October 2023, none approved, per the Israel Planning Council. The rate is no longer low; it is nil.
details.energy_note: Two hundred and eighty-two applications, no approvals at all.

details.aspect: The older baseline, for the trend
details.description: Over 94% of applications between January 2000 and September 2007 were denied. Palestinian construction is effectively prohibited across some 70% of Area C, and restrictions in the remaining 30% virtually eliminate the possibility of a permit.
details.energy_note: A quarter of a century of the same answer.

details.aspect: So the only option is to build without one
details.description: Families build anyway, because children keep being born. The house is then permanently exposed: it carries a demolition order from the day it is finished, and the order may be executed in three years or thirteen.
details.money_note: Cost of a house built knowing it may be demolished.
details.energy_note: A home with a sentence already passed on it.

details.aspect: Which converts a family's entire savings into a hostage
details.description: The house is typically the only substantial asset. Building it is not an investment; it is placing everything the family owns inside a structure the state has already declared unlawful.
details.energy_note: Everything you own, in a building marked for removal.

details.aspect: The permit refusal and the demolition are one policy
details.description: Refusing permits creates the illegality that the demolitions then enforce. Described separately they look like planning and law enforcement; together they are a single mechanism.
details.energy_note: Made illegal, then punished for it.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - Bimkom's five-year count
details.description: Data provided to the Israeli planning rights organisation Bimkom shows that between 2016 and 2020 Palestinians submitted 2,550 building applications in Area C and 24 were approved. Not a low rate applied to a small number - two and a half thousand families, and twenty-four permits.
details.energy_note: Twenty-four approvals in five years.

issues.title: Demolition, at 4.7 structures a day
issues.category_name: Land, home demolition and the building permit nobody gets
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: Demolition for want of a permit is not an occasional event. It runs at a measured daily rate and the rate is rising.

details.aspect: The current rate
details.description: Between 1 January and 30 September 2025, Israeli authorities demolished 1,288 Palestinian structures in the West Bank including East Jerusalem for lack of permits - an average of 4.7 per day, against 929 (3.4/day) in the same period of 2024. 2024's full-year figure was 1,768.
details.energy_note: Nearly five buildings a day, every day.

details.aspect: The people behind the structures
details.description: Those 2025 demolitions displaced 1,414 people and affected 38,017 others - the second figure being wells, sheds, classrooms, clinics, solar panels and access roads that served far more people than lived in them.
details.energy_note: Fourteen hundred homeless, thirty-eight thousand worse off.

details.aspect: The backlog is enormous and deliberate
details.description: The Civil Administration issued over 14,000 demolition orders against Palestinian-owned structures in Area C between 1988 and 2014. An outstanding order is a permanent conditional threat; the uncertainty is itself the instrument.
details.energy_note: Fourteen thousand houses waiting to hear.

details.aspect: You may be billed for your own demolition
details.description: Where authorities carry out the demolition, the costs of the operation can be charged to the owner. Families sometimes demolish their own homes to avoid the fee - and to avoid the bulldozer damaging the neighbours'.
details.money_note: Demolition costs charged to the owner.
details.energy_note: Taking down your own house to get the discount.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the second time
details.description: The first structure went in 2019. They rebuilt in tin and tarpaulin because concrete attracts attention. In 2024 that went too. The third is deliberately temporary - no foundations, nothing that reads as permanent - which also means no insulation, and the children are ill every winter.
details.energy_note: Building worse on purpose, so it hurts less to lose.

details.aspect: The right to challenge is narrowing
details.description: OCHA titled its 2025 reporting on this a peak in demolitions 'amidst increasing denial of the right to justice' - the review routes are closing at the same time as the demolitions accelerate.
details.energy_note: More demolitions, fewer ways to object.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the 2024 to 2025 acceleration
details.description: 1,288 structures demolished for lack of permits between 1 January and 30 September 2025 - 4.7 a day - against 929 in the same period of 2024, which was 3.4 a day. The 2024 full-year figure was 1,768.
details.energy_note: Three point four a day, then four point seven.

issues.title: Punitive demolition: the family pays for the accused
issues.category_name: Land, home demolition and the building permit nobody gets
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: Separately from permit demolitions, homes are demolished as punishment for an attack allegedly committed by a family member - frequently before any trial, and always against people not accused of anything.

details.aspect: The scale
details.description: Between January and September 2025, Israeli authorities carried out 37 punitive demolitions of homes belonging to Palestinians accused of attacks.
details.energy_note: Thirty-seven families evicted for someone else's alleged act.

details.aspect: The people who lose the house are not the accused
details.description: A mother, sisters, grandparents and children lose the home for an act attributed to one member. It is collective punishment by design - the deterrent only works if innocent people are harmed.
details.energy_note: Punished, explicitly, for being related to him.

details.aspect: It often precedes conviction
details.description: Demolition can follow the accusation rather than the verdict, so the sanction is executed before guilt is determined and cannot be undone if it is not.
details.energy_note: The sentence carried out before the trial.

details.aspect: It falls hardest on the women of the household
details.description: Where men are detained or killed, the surviving household is often women and children, and it is they who are present when the building comes down and who must find somewhere that night.
details.energy_note: The house comes down on whoever is still in it.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - thirty-seven households in nine months
details.description: Between January and September 2025 Israeli authorities carried out 37 punitive demolitions of homes belonging to Palestinians accused of attacks - a sanction applied to the household rather than to the accused, and frequently before any conviction.
details.energy_note: Thirty-seven families, for what a relative was accused of.

issues.title: Settler violence at five incidents a day
issues.category_name: Settler violence and the segregated road regime
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: Attacks by settlers on Palestinian people and property reached the highest levels OCHA has recorded since it began counting in 2006, and the UN human rights office finds they occur with the acquiescence or participation of security forces.

details.aspect: The record month and the record year
details.description: October 2025: 264 settler attacks causing casualties, property damage or both - the highest monthly total since records began in 2006, about eight a day. Across 2025: 1,680 attacks in more than 270 communities, an average of five a day.
details.energy_note: Five attacks a day, across two hundred and seventy villages.

details.aspect: The state's posture, per the UN
details.description: In July 2025 the UN human rights office warned that escalating settler violence is carried out 'with the acquiescence, support, and in some cases participation, of Israeli security forces'.
details.energy_note: Not a failure to police it. A decision not to.

details.aspect: Reporting it costs more than it returns
details.description: A complaint means travelling to a police station inside a settlement or military base, often requiring coordination to reach, to file a case with a very low prosecution rate. Most people stop bothering, which then appears in the statistics as fewer incidents.
details.energy_note: A day's journey to file a report that goes nowhere.

details.aspect: For women the risk changes what is possible alone
details.description: Walking to the fields, to school, to the next village becomes something not done alone or after dark. The restriction is informal, unenforced by anyone, and absolute in practice.
details.energy_note: A curfew nobody announced and everybody keeps.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the worst month since records began
details.description: OCHA documented 264 settler attacks causing casualties, property damage or both in October 2025 - the highest monthly total since it began recording in 2006, about eight a day - within a 2025 total of 1,680 attacks across more than 270 communities.
details.energy_note: Eight a day, in the worst month on record.

issues.title: The olive harvest, and being let onto your own land for one day
issues.category_name: Settler violence and the segregated road regime
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: The harvest is both the agricultural year and the cultural one. It now runs under a coordination regime that grants access late, briefly, and to a fraction of the land.

details.aspect: Harvest-season attacks
details.description: 178 olive-harvest-related attacks across 88 communities in October and November 2025. Between 1 October and 3 November alone, 150 harvest attacks injured more than 140 Palestinians and damaged over 4,200 trees and saplings across 77 villages. Up to 2023 OCHA recorded roughly 30 to 60 incidents a season.
details.energy_note: Four thousand trees, in five weeks.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - Tarqumiya: 500 dunums of 5,000, for one day
details.description: Where army permits are required to reach the land, coordination came very late and for one or two days only. In Tarqumiya, access was granted for a single day covering 500 of over 5,000 previously accessible dunums. In Bani Na'im, accessible land fell from about 150 dunums to 12.
details.money_note: Value of a harvest that could not be picked.
details.energy_note: One day, one tenth of the grove, and the rest rots.

details.aspect: An olive tree is a thirty-year asset
details.description: A burned or uprooted tree is not a season's loss. Replacement takes a decade to bear and a generation to mature, so the damage is priced wrongly by everyone who records it as annual.
details.money_note: Per tree, over its productive life.
details.energy_note: Thirty years, in an afternoon.

details.aspect: It is a family and female labour economy
details.description: The harvest is the one agricultural activity involving the whole household, women prominently. Losing access removes an income, a food source, and the annual event around which the extended family assembles.
details.energy_note: Losing the harvest and the family gathering with it.

issues.title: Impunity, and what it does to the arithmetic
issues.category_name: Settler violence and the segregated road regime
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: Where attacks are rarely prosecuted, the cost-benefit facing both the attacker and the victim changes permanently, and the victim's rational response looks from outside like passivity.

details.aspect: Yesh Din's long-run finding
details.description: Israeli monitoring organisations have tracked investigation outcomes in settler-violence cases for two decades and consistently find that only a small fraction of complaints lead to indictment.
details.energy_note: Filing is a formality, and everyone involved knows it.

details.aspect: Self-defence is prosecuted
details.description: Responding physically to an attack is very likely to result in arrest and a military court prosecution with a near-certain conviction. The asymmetry is the thing that has to be internalised.
details.energy_note: Being hit is free. Hitting back is years.

details.aspect: So the adaptation is withdrawal
details.description: Families stop going to the outlying plots, stop letting children walk, stop grazing the far pasture. Land goes unused, and unused land is more easily declared state land.
details.energy_note: Retreating inch by inch, and losing the inches.

details.aspect: Which is the mechanism, not a side effect
details.description: Violence that goes unpunished transfers land more cheaply than any legal process. It does not need to be ordered by anyone to function as policy.
details.energy_note: Dispossession that requires no paperwork.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the UN's finding on who is standing there
details.description: In July 2025 the UN human rights office warned that escalating settler violence is carried out 'with the acquiescence, support, and in some cases participation, of Israeli security forces' - which is the mechanism by which the impunity in this issue operates.
details.energy_note: Not unpoliced. Accompanied.

issues.title: Administrative detention: held on material you cannot see
issues.category_name: Detention, military courts and the prison system
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: Detention without charge or trial, on secret evidence, for renewable six-month periods with no limit on renewals. There is no allegation to answer because none is made.

details.aspect: The mechanism
details.description: Detainees are held on military intelligence material they cannot access, for six months at a time, indefinitely renewable. It is very rarely used against Jewish Israelis.
details.energy_note: Imprisoned by a document nobody will show you.

details.aspect: The current numbers
details.description: More than 22,000 administrative detention orders, new and renewed, since the start of the Gaza war. Administrative detainees rose from roughly 1,300 before the war to more than 3,300 by August 2026.
details.energy_note: Three thousand people, no charges between them.

details.aspect: Appeal is effectively decorative
details.description: The Palestine Center for Prisoners Studies reports that 99% of appeals filed by administrative detainees against extensions are rejected, including by the Supreme Court, often without explanation.
details.energy_note: A one per cent process.

details.aspect: The renewal is the cruelty
details.description: Each period ends with a date the family has counted down to, and can be extended on that day. The release date is real enough to plan around and provisional enough to evaporate.
details.energy_note: Told he's out in March. Told again in September.

details.aspect: The household outside reorganises around it
details.description: A wife becomes the sole earner, sole parent, sole negotiator with lawyers and the sole point of contact for the prison service, indefinitely and with no date at which it resolves.
details.money_note: Lost household income plus legal and visit costs.
details.energy_note: Married, and running the house alone, for years.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the fourth renewal
details.description: She has explained to the children three times that their father is coming home next month. The fourth time she does not tell them the date at all, and the eldest works out why.
details.energy_note: Learning not to tell your children good news.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the scale since October 2023
details.description: More than 22,000 administrative detention orders, new and renewed, have been issued since the start of the Gaza war, with the number of administrative detainees rising from roughly 1,300 before the war to more than 3,300 by August 2026. Riyad al-Ashqar of the Palestine Center for Prisoners Studies said 99% of appeals against extensions are rejected, often without explanation.
details.energy_note: Twenty-two thousand orders, and a one per cent appeal rate.

issues.title: A court system with a conviction rate above 99%
issues.category_name: Detention, military courts and the prison system
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: West Bank Palestinians are tried by military courts. The conviction rate is such that the trial is not meaningfully a contest, and every strategy is built around plea rather than defence.

details.aspect: The rate
details.description: The US State Department's 2013 human rights report found Palestinians tried in Israeli military courts were convicted more than 99% of the time. Other reporting cites 99.7% for West Bank civilians.
details.energy_note: A court that has essentially one outcome.

details.aspect: Which makes pleading guilty the rational choice
details.description: When acquittal is statistically negligible, a plea for a shorter certain sentence beats a trial for a longer near-certain one. The system therefore generates guilty pleas from people who would contest the facts.
details.energy_note: Confessing because arithmetic says to.

details.aspect: Civilians in a military system
details.description: Critics argue trying civilians in military tribunals violates international law and routinely disregards due process. The judges, prosecutors and rules all belong to the party that made the arrest.
details.energy_note: Everyone in the room works for the other side.

details.aspect: Families often do not learn the charge
details.description: Families and institutions frequently receive little information regarding the charges, so the household organises around a sentence whose basis it has never been told.
details.energy_note: Serving a sentence nobody explained.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the figure in a US government report
details.description: The 2013 US State Department human rights report found Palestinians tried in Israeli military courts were convicted more than 99% of the time. The figure comes from the government of Israel's closest ally, not from a critic.
details.energy_note: Ninety-nine per cent, per the State Department.

issues.title: Women in detention
issues.category_name: Detention, military courts and the prison system
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
issues.summary: Women detainees face the general conditions plus a set of specific ones - strip searches, menstrual management with no supplies, and the certainty that detention itself will follow them socially afterwards.

details.aspect: Documented conditions
details.description: Testimonies from released women describe strip searches, threats, sleep deprivation and severe overcrowding, with some sleeping on the floor. Data from Palestinian monitoring bodies indicates 88 women held in Damon prison under difficult humanitarian and health conditions.
details.energy_note: Eighty-eight women, and the floor.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - eight days, no shower, no pads
details.description: One woman described being moved between prisons, subjected to repeated strip searches and interrogations at gunpoint, and during eight days at an unknown facility having no access to a shower, menstrual pads or toiletries.
details.energy_note: Menstruating, in custody, with nothing.

details.aspect: The strip search is used as a routine, not an exception
details.description: Repeated searches on transfer, on return from court, before and after visits. Frequency converts a security procedure into something else.
details.energy_note: Searched so often it stops being about finding anything.

details.aspect: Students are specifically targeted
details.description: The Palestinian Prisoner's Society notes a longstanding policy of targeting university students, particularly women - four Birzeit students were arrested in overnight raids in a single operation.
details.energy_note: Arrested for being enrolled.

details.aspect: Release is not the end of it
details.description: A former female detainee carries a social cost on return - questions about what happened in custody, effects on marriage prospects, and a reluctance in the community to ask or be told. The silence protects nobody.
details.energy_note: Out of prison, into everyone's imagination.

issues.title: No conjugal visits, and what people did about it
issues.category_name: Detention, military courts and the prison system
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
issues.summary: Israel does not grant conjugal visits to Palestinian security prisoners. The response - smuggling sperm out for IVF - is one of the strangest and best-documented adaptations in this dataset, and the state has moved against the children it produced.

details.aspect: The rule that created the practice
details.description: No conjugal visits are granted to Palestinian security prisoners. For a wife whose husband is serving decades, that is a decision about her fertility made by a prison service.
details.energy_note: Your reproductive life, administered by a jail.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the first one
details.description: Ammar Ziben, serving 32 life sentences, smuggled a sample to his wife. Their son Mohannad was born by caesarean on 13 August 2012 at the Razan fertility clinic in Nablus, and the case opened the way for dozens of other prisoners' wives.
details.energy_note: Thirty-two life sentences, and a son.

details.aspect: The clinic, and the numbers
details.description: Razan in Nablus received one or two smuggled samples a week in 2013, kept about 65 frozen at -196C and had put 22 women through IVF. Counts of babies born vary by date: 32 over three years, about 50 by early 2018, over 60 by late 2018, some 120 in a little over a decade. ICSI is used because the samples arrive degraded.
details.money_note: IVF/ICSI cycle costs.
details.energy_note: Sixty-plus children, conceived through a prison wall.
details.notes: The clinic's director refused funding from both Hamas and Fatah, saying the interest was humanitarian rather than political.

details.aspect: The state's response was to deny the children papers
details.description: Israel has denied identification documents or legal status to babies born this way, and those children are denied visits to their imprisoned fathers. Surveillance cameras were installed in cells and visitation was tightened after births peaked in 2015.
details.energy_note: A child with no papers, barred from meeting his father.

details.aspect: The woman carries the reputational risk
details.description: Families and friends are deliberately involved in the process so that the wife's reputation is protected and the community accepts the child is the result of science rather than sin. The protection has to be organised in advance because the suspicion is assumed.
details.energy_note: Arranging witnesses to your own pregnancy.

details.aspect: It is simultaneously a private decision and a public statement
details.description: The births are reported, dedicated, and read politically by everyone. A woman's decision to have a child becomes a national event she did not necessarily want to host.
details.energy_note: Your pregnancy, on the news.

issues.title: The medical permit, and the difference between denial and silence
issues.category_name: Health access, referrals and the medical permit
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: Specialist care is largely outside Gaza and outside the West Bank's reach, so treatment requires an exit permit. The permit is rarely refused outright; it is more often simply not answered before the appointment passes.

details.aspect: The approval rate, and its collapse
details.description: Patient permit approvals through Erez fell from 92.5% in 2012 to 88.7% in 2013, 82.4% in 2014 and 77.5% in 2015. In May 2017 only 47.2% were approved; the January-October 2017 average was 54%. It recovered to 85% by February 2023 and 81% in July 2023.
details.energy_note: Your odds depend on the year you got ill.

details.aspect: Denial is rare. Delay is the instrument
details.description: In May 2017, of 2,282 applications, 1,077 were approved, only 47 were denied - and 1,158, over half, were left without a response by the date of the appointment. Among them 255 children under 18 and 141 people over 60.
details.energy_note: Not refused. Just answered too late to matter.

details.aspect: A missed appointment is not rescheduled cheaply
details.description: The referral, the hospital slot and the permit must line up simultaneously. Missing one means restarting all three, and the disease does not pause for the administration.
details.energy_note: Three clocks, and they have to chime together.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the sixth application
details.description: Her oncologist referred her in March. The first request went unanswered, the second was answered in May for an April appointment, the third and fourth went unanswered. By the sixth the staging has changed and the protocol with it.
details.energy_note: A different cancer by the time the paper came.
details.notes: Constructed, but Gisha documents a real case of six separate requests by a young woman awaiting urgent cancer treatment.

details.aspect: The permit regime is a health determinant
details.description: Survival for time-sensitive disease depends on an administrative response time that is not published, not guaranteed and not appealable. It belongs in the clinical record and appears in nobody's.
details.energy_note: A prognosis that includes a government's response time.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - May 2017, the month the system stopped answering
details.description: Of 2,282 patient applications that month, 1,077 were approved and only 47 refused - while 1,158, more than half, received no response at all by the date of the appointment. Among them were 255 children under 18 and 141 people aged over 60.
details.energy_note: Two hundred and fifty-five children, no answer.

issues.title: Travelling to treatment alone
issues.category_name: Health access, referrals and the medical permit
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
issues.summary: A patient may be approved while the person who would accompany her is not. For children, the elderly and women travelling to unfamiliar cities, the companion permit is the one that decides whether the journey happens.

details.aspect: Companions are refused at far higher rates than patients
