details.energy_note: The numbers are real. The explanation offered is not.

details.aspect: Cause and characteristic get swapped
details.description: A fishery restricted to 15% of its water, a manufacturing sector without electricity, a workforce without permits and an import regime that bans pumps, will produce exactly these figures in any population on earth.
details.energy_note: Any people, under this, would show these numbers.

details.aspect: And aid dependency is then held against them
details.description: Receiving aid is treated as a disposition rather than an outcome, which supports the argument for restricting the aid, which deepens the dependency.
details.energy_note: Blamed for needing what you were made to need.

details.aspect: This is the bridge into the psychological section
details.description: Everything in PSY rests on this row: the conditions are imposed, the resulting statistics are attributed to the character of the people, and the person then carries that attribution into every room she enters abroad.
details.energy_note: Carrying a reputation manufactured by a blockade.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the figures that get quoted without their cause
details.description: 57% of Gaza households food insecure, about 80% aid recipients, 34.5% unemployment among those able and willing to work. The fishery was restricted to 15% of its water, manufacturing had 5-7 hours of power, and water and sewage pumps were on the restricted-import list.
details.energy_note: The statistics, and the policy that produced them, in one row.

issues.title: Thirty-nine professions you may not enter
issues.category_name: Refugee status abroad: Lebanon, Jordan, Syria, the Gulf
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: In Lebanon, Palestinian refugees are barred from dozens of syndicated professions. The bar is not on ability or qualification; it is on the category the person was born into.

details.aspect: The bar
details.description: UNRWA states Palestine refugees in Lebanon face a prohibition on working in 39 professions. A UN Special Rapporteur noted exclusion from syndicated professions such as law, medicine and engineering 'may be seen as prima facie discriminatory'.
details.energy_note: Qualified as a doctor, forbidden to practise.

details.aspect: The mechanism underneath it
details.description: Decree No. 17561 of 1964 governs employment of foreign workers and requires non-Lebanese including Palestinians to obtain work permits under conditions often impossible to meet. National preference rules plus the permit requirement make formal employment practically impossible, confining refugees to low-paid informal work with no labour or social protection.
details.energy_note: Permitted in principle, impossible in procedure.

details.aspect: The reforms that did not reach
details.description: In 2005 Lebanon lifted a ban on most clerical and technical posts subject to a temporary permit, but more than 20 high-level professions remained closed - medicine, law, engineering, pharmacy. 2010 amendments reduced some fees and eased reciprocity, with limited implementation.
details.energy_note: Two reforms, and the same professions still closed.

details.aspect: The employment outcome
details.description: A 2010 study found just 37% of working-age Palestinians in Lebanon were employed. Those working illegally face wage discrimination - many employers pay less than Lebanese colleagues or refuse to hire at all.
details.money_note: Annual earnings gap versus a Lebanese peer.
details.energy_note: Thirty-seven per cent of adults, working.

details.aspect: It makes education a strange investment
details.description: Families still educate children who will not be permitted to practise. The degree becomes an emigration ticket or an ornament, and everyone involved knows it while doing it.
details.energy_note: A medical degree you'll never be allowed to use here.

details.aspect: For women it compounds an already low participation rate
details.description: Where formal work is closed and informal work is male-dominated manual labour, the remaining options for women narrow to domestic and piecework at the lowest rates in the economy.
details.energy_note: Excluded twice - as a refugee, then as a woman.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the 2005 reform that left the professions closed
details.description: In 2005 Lebanon lifted a ban on most clerical and technical positions subject to a temporary work permit, but more than 20 high-level professions remained off-limits - medicine, law, engineering and pharmacy among them. 2010 amendments reduced some fees and eased reciprocity requirements, with limited implementation.
details.energy_note: Two reforms, and the doctors still cannot practise.

issues.title: Not being allowed to own the home you live in
issues.category_name: Refugee status abroad: Lebanon, Jordan, Syria, the Gulf
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Lebanon's 2001 property law bars Palestinians from owning real estate, using a formula that never names them.

details.aspect: The drafting trick
details.description: Law No. 296 of 2001, revising Legislative Decree No. 11614 of 1969, prohibits 'any person who is not a national of a recognized state' from acquiring real estate of any kind. It does not mention Palestinians and applies to almost nobody else.
details.energy_note: A law about statelessness, aimed at one people.

details.aspect: They had the right before
details.description: Palestinians had held property rights in Lebanon for decades before 2001. This was a removal, not a continuation.
details.energy_note: A right they had, taken back.

details.aspect: The constitutional challenge failed
details.description: Parliamentarians petitioned the Constitutional Council to review the clause as a breach of constitutional bans on discrimination. The petition failed and the Council affirmed the clause.
details.energy_note: Challenged, and upheld.

details.aspect: No property means no inheritance and no collateral
details.description: Three generations of work cannot be converted into an asset, passed to a child, or borrowed against to start anything. The family's savings have nowhere to become capital.
details.money_note: Value of a lifetime's housing equity never accrued.
details.energy_note: Seventy years of rent and nothing to leave anyone.

details.aspect: The stated purpose is to prevent settlement
details.description: The aim is widely acknowledged to be preventing permanent settlement of Palestinians in Lebanon. The instrument for preventing permanence is to make seventy years of residence produce nothing.
details.energy_note: Kept temporary, on purpose, for three generations.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - Law 296 of 2001, and the words it uses
details.description: The law prohibits 'any person who is not a national of a recognized state' from acquiring real estate of any kind. It never names Palestinians and applies to almost no one else. Parliamentarians petitioned the Constitutional Council to strike it as discriminatory; the petition failed and the Council affirmed the clause.
details.energy_note: A sentence with no Palestinians in it, aimed at Palestinians.

issues.title: A status you inherit and cannot exit
issues.category_name: Refugee status abroad: Lebanon, Jordan, Syria, the Gulf
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Host states have largely declined naturalisation as a matter of policy, and the status passes to children, so the condition compounds rather than resolving.

details.aspect: The policy, stated regionally
details.description: Recipient states largely do not permit naturalisation, granting neither citizenship nor residency documents despite long residence - Lebanon, Syria, Egypt and the Gulf. Jordan is the exception, following its 1948 annexation.
details.energy_note: Seventy-eight years, still a guest.
details.notes: Most directly stated in Russian-language coverage; English sources tend to describe it country by country rather than as a regional rule.

details.aspect: The camps, and who runs them
details.description: 59 recognised camps across Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, the West Bank and Gaza. Camps require host-state consent to exist; UNRWA provides services but does not administer them. Registered refugees went from about 750,000 in 1950 to over 5.6 million by 2019, over 1.5 million of them in camps.
details.energy_note: A temporary camp with a seventy-year lease.

details.aspect: The first thing a camp child is told is where they are from
details.description: Camps in Lebanon, Syria, Jordan and the West Bank were organised by village of origin, and children born there are told their home village first. Identity is transmitted deliberately because the alternative is dissolution.
details.energy_note: Born in Beirut, from a village you've never seen.

details.aspect: And expulsion is a recurring event
details.description: After the 1991 Gulf War, Jordan received Palestinians expelled from Gulf states. A population without citizenship anywhere can be removed from anywhere, and periodically is.
details.energy_note: Deportable from every country you've lived in.

details.aspect: Refusal to absorb is also a political position held by the refugees
details.description: Host states refuse naturalisation partly to preserve the right of return, a position many Palestinians share. The person living the consequence is therefore caught between a principle she may believe in and a life she cannot build.
details.energy_note: A principle you agree with, costing you a country.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - 59 camps, and who is allowed to run them
details.description: UNRWA recognises 59 camps across Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, the West Bank and Gaza. Camps require the host state's consent to exist, and UNRWA provides services without administering them. Registered refugees rose from about 750,000 in 1950 to over 5.6 million by 2019.
details.energy_note: Fifty-nine camps, and a number that only goes up.

issues.title: Being refused as a refugee, again
issues.category_name: Refugee status abroad: Lebanon, Jordan, Syria, the Gulf
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: When displacement recurs, the neighbouring states publicly refuse to receive the displaced - which is itself a message received by the people being bombed.

details.aspect: The refusals, stated at head-of-state level
details.description: Egypt said it would not solve regional problems at its own expense and would not receive refugees from Gaza; President Sisi stated this on 21 October 2023. King Abdullah II called sending Palestinian refugees to Jordan a 'red line', saying 'No refugees in Jordan, no refugees in Egypt.'
details.energy_note: Two neighbours, publicly, on the record.

details.aspect: The reason is not indifference and does not help
details.description: The refusal rests on refusing to complete a displacement that would be permanent. The reasoning is coherent and the effect on a family under bombardment is that there is nowhere to go.
details.energy_note: Refused entry for your own long-term good.

details.aspect: 'Palestinians do not dissolve into the Arab sea'
details.description: The regional framing - that Palestinians are not to be absorbed - is protective of the claim and total in its cost to the individual, who is a person and not a claim.
details.energy_note: A nation's rights, paid for by one woman's week.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - two heads of state, on the record
details.description: President Sisi stated on 21 October 2023 that Egypt would not accept the relocation of Gazans to Sinai. King Abdullah II called sending Palestinian refugees to Jordan a red line: 'No refugees in Jordan, no refugees in Egypt.'
details.energy_note: Both neighbours, publicly, in the same week.

issues.title: A database built to stop you being employed
issues.category_name: Diaspora, speech and the professional cost of the identity
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Doxxing operations publish profiles of students and academics with the explicitly stated purpose of preventing their future employment, and internally track firings as a performance metric.

details.aspect: The stated aim, in their own words
details.description: Canary Mission has published thousands of profiles, primarily of students and professors, since 2015, stating its aim is to 'ensure that today's radicals are not tomorrow's employees'.
details.energy_note: A project whose stated product is your unemployment.

details.aspect: The mechanism is search results
details.description: An employer searching a candidate's name encounters the accusations first, and few will investigate further. Palestine Legal reports numerous students questioned by employers and graduate schools about their profiles.
details.money_note: Lifetime earnings effect of a poisoned search result.
details.energy_note: Your name, permanently, first result.

details.aspect: They count the firings as output
details.description: Internal reporting indicates a non-public Canary-linked site, BlackNest, categorises impacts into 'change of behaviour', job loss, denials of entry to the US, arrests, and 'deportation/forced to flee' - tracked as 'company impact' metrics.
details.energy_note: Your deportation, logged as a KPI.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - filmed, profiled, fired
details.description: Laila Ali was filmed taking down flyers, had a profile posted the next day, and was fired from the mental health clinic where she worked. The lawsuit says her employer was flooded with coordinated calls and emails demanding her termination, and StopAntisemitism later thanked the employer for firing her.
details.energy_note: Twenty-four hours from a video to no job.

details.aspect: The scale claimed
details.description: StopAntisemitism's founder claims over 1,000 people profiled and over 400 fired. A CAIR Chicago class action claims over 300 Illinois residents were doxed, detailing threatened or lost jobs, suppressed speech and jeopardised safety.
details.energy_note: Four hundred jobs, claimed as an achievement.

details.aspect: Institutions have noticed and that is all
details.description: Universities such as Berkeley have issued statements discouraging use of these sites as employment vetting tools because of chilling effects. A statement discouraging use is not a mechanism preventing it.
details.energy_note: Officially discouraged, practically universal.

details.aspect: The rational response is to never say anything, ever
details.description: Given a permanent searchable record and a documented employment effect, the risk-minimising strategy for a 19-year-old is total silence on the subject of her own family's history.
details.energy_note: Silent about your own grandmother, for your CV.
details.notes: See PSY-003.

issues.title: Being the designated explainer
issues.category_name: Diaspora, speech and the professional cost of the identity
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: During any escalation, every colleague and acquaintance treats the nearest Palestinian as a spokesperson, an explanation service or a proxy defendant.

details.aspect: The question is never neutral
details.description: 'So what do you think about what's happening?' - asked in a kitchen, by someone with a position already formed, of a person whose cousin is not answering their phone.
details.energy_note: A debate, while you are waiting for a text.

details.aspect: Every available answer is costly
details.description: Speak and be marked as political. Decline and be read as evasive or as endorsing something. There is no response that returns the conversation to the work you were doing.
details.energy_note: Three answers, all of them wrong.

details.aspect: It removes work as a refuge
details.description: The one place that was a functioning distraction becomes another site of it. People take leave they cannot afford, or go quiet in ways that damage their standing.
details.energy_note: Losing the only room it wasn't in.

details.aspect: And withdrawal is then held against you
details.description: The predictable response is retreat into the co-national community, which is then cited as a failure to integrate.
details.energy_note: Withdrawn for cause, and blamed for withdrawing.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - deportation proposed before any charge
details.description: The Berlin Senate sought to deport four pro-Palestinian activists over an occupation at the Free University while investigations were still running. None had been charged or convicted. Three were EU nationals and one American; legal analysis held the expulsions probably unlawful.
details.energy_note: An expulsion order, ahead of the charge.

issues.title: The cost of a name on a CV
issues.category_name: Diaspora, speech and the professional cost of the identity
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Before any speech, the name alone does work in a hiring process, a tenancy application and a security clearance.

details.aspect: It is never stated and never has to be
details.description: No rejection says why. The effect is only visible in aggregate, and no individual can ever demonstrate it happened to her.
details.energy_note: Never rejected for it. Never hired either.

details.aspect: Clearance and export-control roles are structurally closed
details.description: Defence-adjacent, government and some technical roles apply origin-linked screening that excludes candidates with certain birthplaces and family ties, lawfully and without explanation.
details.energy_note: Whole industries, quietly out of reach.

details.aspect: Some people change the name
details.description: Shortening, anglicising or using a middle name measurably improves callback rates and costs something that is not measured anywhere.
details.energy_note: Getting the interview by not being yourself.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - what the doxxing site says it is for
details.description: Canary Mission has stated since 2015 that its aim is to 'ensure that today's radicals are not tomorrow's employees'. The employment effect is not an unintended consequence of the profiles; it is the stated product.
details.energy_note: The purpose, in their own sentence.

issues.title: Sending money back, and what it takes
issues.category_name: Diaspora, speech and the professional cost of the identity
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Remittance is the mechanism through which obligation, guilt and power are negotiated in a family split by a border - and the payment rails make it expensive and legally exposed.

details.aspect: The obligation has no ceiling
details.description: Whatever is sent, more is needed, because prices move and the needs are medical. There is no amount that discharges it.
details.money_note: Annual remittance load.
details.energy_note: A bill never paid in full.

details.aspect: The transfer costs a premium and carries risk
details.description: Formal channels are restricted, so transfers run through informal networks at a spread, with counterparty risk and legal exposure at both ends.
details.energy_note: A fee and a legal risk, to send your mother her rent.

details.aspect: It delays the sender's own life by a decade
details.description: Deposit, pension, training, children - deferred to fund a household abroad. Measured at sixty, the remittance decade is not recoverable.
details.energy_note: Your thirties, spent on someone else's survival.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the freelance payout gap
details.description: On Upwork, Palestinian freelancers often lose a further 20-30% of earnings to currency-exchange intermediaries on top of platform fees, because the standard payout rails - PayPal and Payoneer - exclude them while serving Israeli settlers in the same territory.
details.energy_note: A quarter of every invoice, to get it at all.

issues.title: The watchlist, and whose names are on it
issues.category_name: Airports abroad, screening and the watchlist
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Airport screening in the US runs on name-based watchlist matching. The best available analysis of the list's composition indicates it is overwhelmingly Muslim names, which makes 'random' additional screening statistically anything but.

details.aspect: The composition of the list
details.description: CAIR analysed a 2019 FBI watchlist copy leaked after a regional air carrier accidentally posted it - over 1.5 million entries. The top 50 most frequently occurring names were all Muslim names, and CAIR estimated over 1.47 million entries, more than 98%, regarded Muslims. A separate analysis of the same leak found more than 10% of entries - 174,202 of 1,566,062 - contain 'MUHAMMAD' in the first or last name field.
details.energy_note: A million and a half names, and the top fifty are all Muslim.
details.source_name: CAIR analysis of leaked 2019 TSDB copy
details.notes: HONEST CAVEAT: this is advocacy-organisation analysis of a leaked file, not official data. It is the best available because no official demographic breakdown is published.

details.aspect: Why name-matching hits this group hardest
details.description: Screening is name-based, so people not on the list who have names resembling listed ones get misidentified. The effect is pronounced for travellers with common surnames and from backgrounds where name similarity is more likely - which describes Arabic naming conventions precisely.
details.energy_note: Flagged for having a common name in the wrong language.

details.aspect: SSSS, and what it costs each time
details.description: Secondary Security Screening Selection printed on a boarding pass means the passenger and all their belongings are searched. Time in secondary can run to several hours, depending partly on how easily it can be verified that the person is not the one on the list.
details.money_note: Missed connections, rebooked flights, per occurrence.
details.energy_note: Four hours, every flight, for years.

details.aspect: The false-positive volume was large enough for DHS to concede it
details.description: A then-DHS Secretary cited one major US airline recording 9,000 false positives. DHS has acknowledged that people mistakenly listed or misidentified can face consequences 'ranging from inconvenience and delay to loss of liberty'.
details.energy_note: Nine thousand wrong flags, at one airline.

details.aspect: HONEST GAP - there is no published per-ethnicity selection rate
details.description: TSA does not publish an SSSS selection rate broken down by ethnicity or national origin. The claim that Palestinians are selected at an unusually high rate is supported by the list's composition and by consistent community reporting, not by an official statistic, because that statistic does not exist.
details.energy_note: Everyone knows the rate. Nobody publishes it.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - 174,202 entries containing one name
details.description: Analysis of a leaked 2019 copy of the FBI watchlist found more than 10% of entries - 174,202 of 1,566,062 - contained 'MUHAMMAD' in the first or last name field, and that the 50 most frequently occurring names on the list were all Muslim names. The screening is name-based, so the commonest names carry the highest false-positive exposure.
details.energy_note: One name, in a hundred and seventy-four thousand records.
details.notes: Advocacy analysis of a leaked file. No official demographic breakdown is published, which is itself recorded in AIR-001.

issues.title: Held at the border with a valid visa
issues.category_name: Airports abroad, screening and the watchlist
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: A visa is permission to travel to a port of entry, not to enter. Recent cases show Palestinians with valid documents held for days, without counsel, with no reason given.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - nine days in a screening room at Houston
details.description: Muhanad J. M. Alshrouf, 22, was held nine days in a secondary screening room at George Bush Intercontinental despite entering on a valid immigrant visa after a years-long process, arriving 5 July 2025 to visit his US-citizen father. Advocates said he had no criminal record and had passed background checks by both US and Israeli authorities. His attorney noted CBP's own policy requires processing within 72 hours; no reason was given and he was denied access to counsel. He was released hours after CAIR alerted the press.
details.energy_note: Nine days in a room, for nothing, with a valid visa.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - visas revoked on arrival at SFO
details.description: Two Palestinian humanitarian activists invited to speak in the Bay Area were held at San Francisco International; a city supervisor said CBP gave no reason for revoking their visas and indicated the men would be sent back.
details.energy_note: Invited to speak, returned to sender.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - detained returning from her honeymoon
details.description: Ward Sakeik, a Palestinian woman, was detained by ICE while returning from her honeymoon.
details.energy_note: Back from honeymoon, into detention.

details.aspect: CBP's position is the structural answer
details.description: CBP states it cannot discuss individual cases and that a visa does not guarantee entry - an officer at the port of entry determines admissibility. That is legally accurate and means the years of process preceding the flight guarantee nothing.
details.energy_note: Every approval you obtained, overridable at the desk.

details.aspect: There is a community advisory, which is its own datapoint
details.description: CAIR issued a precautionary travel advisory to Palestinian-American Muslim travellers following reports of detentions and invasive questioning, specifically referencing those advocating for Palestinian human rights.
details.energy_note: Your own civil rights body advises caution about coming home.

details.aspect: There is precedent with a different nationality
details.description: In January 2020 more than 80 Americans of Iranian descent were held at length in secondary inspection at the Peace Arch crossing, with nearly 300 reportedly affected, including citizens, permanent residents, elderly people and children.
details.energy_note: The same procedure, a different nationality, five years earlier.
details.notes: Cross-reference: this incident is recorded in assets/text/iran.

issues.title: Redress that does not redress
issues.category_name: Airports abroad, screening and the watchlist
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: The official remedy for repeated wrongful screening is a complaint programme whose effectiveness is contested by the people who use it and by government auditors.

details.aspect: The mechanism
details.description: DHS TRIP is the designated channel for travellers who experience repeated secondary screening, boarding denials, unexplained delays or unusual questioning.
details.energy_note: There is a form. That is the remedy.

details.aspect: And its contested effectiveness
details.description: Many frequent fliers report their TRIP appeals have not helped. DHS OIG reporting has noted mismatches affecting low-risk travellers with redress mechanisms not fully mitigating false positives.
details.energy_note: Filed, acknowledged, and screened again next month.

details.aspect: You cannot find out whether you are listed
details.description: There is no route to confirm listing or learn the reason. Litigation has been the only mechanism - CAIR's Baby Doe v. Piehota was brought by 19 plaintiffs to find out why they were on the list at all.
details.energy_note: Suing to be told whether you are on a list.

details.aspect: So you build your life around the assumption
details.description: Arrive four hours early. Never book a tight connection. Never check a bag you need. Never travel the day before something that matters. The adaptation is permanent and costs money on every trip.
details.money_note: Annual cost of defensive travel planning.
details.energy_note: Planning every journey around a search.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - suing in order to be told
details.description: There is no route to confirm whether you are listed or why. Litigation has been the only mechanism: CAIR's Baby Doe v. Piehota was brought by 19 plaintiffs against DHS, the FBI, TSA and the Terrorist Screening Center simply to find out why they were on the watchlist.
details.energy_note: Nineteen people, in federal court, asking why.

issues.title: The exit interview at your own departure
issues.category_name: Airports abroad, screening and the watchlist
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Departing from Ben Gurion - for those few permitted - and from several regional airports involves an interrogation calibrated to origin, conducted in public, with luggage opened in front of the queue.

details.aspect: The questioning is the procedure, not a response to anything
details.description: Who packed the bag, who did you meet, what is your father's name, your grandfather's name, why is your Arabic better than your Hebrew. The answers do not change the outcome; the process is the point.
details.energy_note: Three hours of questions with no right answer.

details.aspect: It is performed publicly
details.description: Bags opened on a table in front of other passengers, belongings handled, sometimes clothing searched. The humiliation is a component rather than a side effect.
details.energy_note: Your underwear, on a table, in front of the queue.

details.aspect: For women it includes searches that are hard to describe afterwards
details.description: Body searches conducted in side rooms are reported consistently and described rarely, because describing them is its own cost.
details.energy_note: The part of the journey she won't talk about.

details.aspect: It has to be budgeted for
details.description: Arriving four to five hours early is not caution, it is arithmetic. That time is unpaid, repeated, and spent by every member of the family every time they fly.
details.time_note: Cumulative days per year at airports before check-in.
details.energy_note: A working week a year, standing in a terminal.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the document that only works at one airport
details.description: The Israeli laissez-passer held by East Jerusalem Palestinians permits travel only via Israeli airports, while the Jordanian temporary passport most of them also hold cannot be used to transit Ben Gurion. Two documents, each valid for the leg the other cannot cover.
details.energy_note: Two travel documents, one journey, neither sufficient alone.

issues.title: A name with no correct spelling
issues.category_name: Names: transliteration, misspelling and identity mismatch
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Arabic names have no single canonical Latin transliteration, so the same person's name is legitimately spelled several ways across her own documents - and every system that compares documents treats that as a discrepancy.

details.aspect: There is no right answer to copy
details.description: Different professional translators make different legitimate transliteration choices. Maryam on a mother's passport and Mariam on her child's birth certificate triggers questions about whether the documents establish the family relationship at all.
details.energy_note: Your daughter's birth certificate doesn't match you.

details.aspect: Systems that match exact text generate false discrepancies
details.description: Where records hold different transliterations, exact-match systems produce mismatches that delay onboarding, increase manual review and flag legitimate customers - across passports, licences, applications, credit bureaus and watchlists.
details.energy_note: Rejected by a string comparison.

details.aspect: The four-field problem
details.description: Arabic naming convention is first name, father's name, grandfather's name, family name. Systems built for that force two-part names into four fields by splitting or duplicating; systems built for two reject four. Either way the output differs from the input.
details.energy_note: A name that doesn't fit the boxes in either direction.

details.aspect: Downstream failures persist for decades
details.description: Inconsistent names create E-Verify failures, background check mismatches and banking or credit issues that persist long after any immigration status is resolved.
details.energy_note: A typo from 2009, still failing checks in 2026.

details.aspect: And correcting it is slow and charged for
details.description: Correcting a green card error requires Form I-90, cited at $455 and 6-12 months to process - for a mistake made by the agency that issued it.
details.energy_note: Four hundred dollars and a year, for their typo.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - Maryam and Mariam
details.description: A mother's passport spelled Maryam and her child's birth certificate spelled Mariam triggers questions about whether the documents establish the family relationship at all. Both spellings are legitimate transliterations; there is no correct one to have used.
details.energy_note: One letter between you and proving she is your daughter.

issues.title: The identity is frozen before you reach the airport
issues.category_name: Names: transliteration, misspelling and identity mismatch
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Modern air travel locks a vetted identity at booking. A mismatch discovered later cannot be corrected at the gate, by anyone, for technical reasons.

details.aspect: How the lock works
details.description: The booking creates a Passenger Name Record; that generates Secure Flight Passenger Data, sent to government screening before a boarding pass issues. Once vetting completes the identity is frozen; changing a surname means changing the vetted identity, which requires re-vetting that cannot happen in real time.
details.energy_note: Nobody at the airport can fix it. Not a supervisor. Nobody.

details.aspect: And eVisas are bound to the exact MRZ
details.description: Many electronic visas are cryptographically linked to the exact machine-readable zone of the passport, so a minor spelling deviation invalidates the authorisation outright.
details.energy_note: A visa invalidated by one letter.

details.aspect: The defensive practice is unusual diligence
details.description: Copy the spelling from the MRZ, use the same passport for every booking, eVisa, hotel and loyalty profile, and contact the airline before check-in rather than at the airport. This is knowledge most travellers never need.
details.energy_note: Expertise in a system that shouldn't need any.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the hyphen
details.description: Her married surname is hyphenated on the passport and unhyphenated in the airline's 30-character field. She has flown on it eleven times. On the twelfth, a different carrier's system reads it differently and the boarding pass does not issue.
details.energy_note: Eleven flights fine, and the twelfth is a hyphen.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - why nobody at the airport can fix it
details.description: A booking creates a Passenger Name Record, which generates Secure Flight Passenger Data sent to government screening before a boarding pass can issue. Once vetting completes the identity is frozen; changing a surname means changing the vetted identity, which requires re-vetting that cannot happen at the gate. Many eVisas are additionally bound to the exact passport MRZ.
details.energy_note: Not a rule a supervisor can waive. A sequence that cannot be rerun.

issues.title: Being mistaken for someone
issues.category_name: Names: transliteration, misspelling and identity mismatch
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: A false positive against a watchlist or a sanctions list is not a brief inconvenience; it attaches to the person and reappears at every subsequent check.

details.aspect: Banks act first and ask later
details.description: A name match triggers a hold, a review, or a closure. The institution's incentive is to act on a possible match, because the cost of a wrong closure falls entirely on the customer.
details.energy_note: Account frozen over a name you share.

details.aspect: Clearing it is not a thing you can do once
details.description: There is no central register to be removed from and no certificate of innocence to present. Each institution repeats the process independently, forever.
details.energy_note: Proving it again, at every new institution.

details.aspect: The commonest names carry the most risk
details.description: Because 10% of the leaked watchlist entries contain 'Muhammad', the most ordinary names in the population are the ones most exposed. Being unremarkable is the risk factor.
details.energy_note: Penalised for having an ordinary name.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the four-field name
details.description: Arabic naming convention runs first name, father's name, grandfather's name, family name. Systems built for four fields force two-part names to be split or duplicated; systems built for two reject four. Either way the stored name differs from the document, and every later comparison flags it.
details.energy_note: A name that does not fit the form in either direction.

issues.title: The officer who decided, and the one who would not have
issues.category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the officer who decided
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: A large share of these hurdles are not policy. They are one person's decision on one day, which another person on another day would have made differently - and which is then permanent.

details.aspect: Same file, different answer
details.description: The same application, the same documents, a different clerk, a different result. Everyone who deals with these systems knows this and none of them can prove it in their own case.
details.energy_note: Refused by a person who was having a bad morning.

details.aspect: Discretion is unappealable precisely because it is discretion
details.description: Where the decision-maker is entitled to weigh factors, there is no error of law to appeal. Being wrongly assessed is not a ground; being unlawfully assessed is, and the two are hard to distinguish from outside.
details.energy_note: Not wrong enough to appeal, wrong enough to ruin it.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the eligible woman with no insurance
details.description: She is entitled to the coverage. The clerk enters her status incorrectly, the system generates a refusal, and the refusal becomes the record. Eleven months later an ombudsman agrees she was always eligible. The surgery happened in month four, uninsured.
details.energy_note: Correct all along, and bankrupt anyway.

details.aspect: The apology, where it comes, restores nothing
details.description: Systems that correct errors rarely compensate for the interval. The finding that you were right is issued after the consequences have completed.
details.energy_note: Vindicated, too late to matter.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the ban that evaporated twice
details.description: A Gaza physician was refused a permit to reach Palestinian Medical Council exams in Ramallah in 2018 on unspecified security grounds. Gisha petitioned the High Court; the ban was retracted before the hearing and 3,000 ILS costs were awarded against the state. In February 2019 she was refused again, on unspecified security grounds, and the state withdrew immediately after the second petition.
details.energy_note: A security threat twice, and never once in front of a judge.

issues.title: The clerical error that becomes your permanent record
issues.category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the officer who decided
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: A wrong date, a wrong spelling, a wrong status code entered once is copied forward by every subsequent system, and the burden of disproving it is entirely the person's.

details.aspect: Databases copy, they do not verify
details.description: The error propagates from the first record into every downstream system, each of which treats the others as corroboration.
details.energy_note: One typo, confirmed by four systems.

details.aspect: You are presumed to be the unreliable party
details.description: The person asserting the record is wrong is, by default, the one whose account is doubted. Institutions trust their own data over a person standing in front of them.
details.energy_note: Your word against a field in a database.

details.aspect: Correction requires the original, which may not exist
details.description: Fixing it means producing the authoritative source document - from an archive that may have been destroyed, in a jurisdiction that may not answer.
details.energy_note: Fix it by producing a document from a building that's gone.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - punished for a relative's overstay
details.description: In seven petitions filed for Palestinian Christians in Gaza denied permits to visit holy sites and family, the ground cited in all seven cases was 'overstay' - meaning the applicant had a relative who at some point overstayed a permit.
details.energy_note: Seven refusals, seven relatives, no act by the applicant.

issues.title: The letterhead
issues.category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the officer who decided
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: The single most concise illustration in this dataset of bureaucracy as an instrument: a document about a dying man was refused because of the words printed at the top of it.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - 'doesn't transfer documents with the heading State of Palestine'
details.description: Gisha petitioned the Jerusalem District Court for a Gaza resident and her three children to travel to the West Bank to visit her husband, who was undergoing life-threatening surgery, after earlier requests were rejected without explanation. It was agreed Gisha would submit an official Palestinian Health Ministry medical document to COGAT - and the Israeli government then demanded it be routed via the Palestinian Civil Affairs Committee, saying it 'doesn't transfer documents with the heading State of Palestine'. Gisha published the insignia before and after redaction.
details.energy_note: A wife's hospital visit, held up by a logo.

details.aspect: The mechanism is that form is substitutable for substance
details.description: Nothing about the medical facts was in dispute. The objection was to two words in a header, and it worked, because a procedural objection does not have to be proportionate to function.
details.energy_note: An objection to typography, with medical consequences.

details.aspect: Which means no application is ever safely complete
details.description: If the letterhead can be the obstacle, then anything can be. There is no checklist that guarantees a submission is sufficient, so the applicant lives in permanent uncertainty about whether she has done enough.
details.energy_note: No way to know when your paperwork is finished.

details.aspect: It is also the whole conflict, compressed into a stationery dispute
details.description: The refusal to handle a paper bearing the words 'State of Palestine' is not incidental to the permit regime. It is the same position, expressed at the scale of one woman's hospital visit.
details.energy_note: The entire argument, printed at the top of a medical form.

issues.title: Being read as a threat before you speak
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: The identity arrives in the room first and carries a prepackaged meaning assembled by decades of coverage. Everything after that is spent correcting an impression nobody admits to having.

details.aspect: The correction tax
details.description: Every new room - a job, a class, a clinic, a landlord - begins with an unpaid effort to establish that you are not what was assumed. The energy spent there is energy not spent on the actual task.
details.energy_note: Starting every conversation three steps back.

details.aspect: Moderation is read as evidence, and so is anger
details.description: Being measured about it reads as evasive or as proof there is nothing wrong. Being upset about it confirms the stereotype. There is no register in which the subject can be discussed without cost.
details.energy_note: Calm proves it's fine. Angry proves them right.

details.aspect: Women carry a doubled version
details.description: Simultaneously assumed to be oppressed and to be threatening - pitied for a culture and suspected for a politics, often by the same person in the same conversation.
details.energy_note: Pitied and suspected, at once, by the same colleague.

details.aspect: It is unfalsifiable, which is what makes it exhausting
details.description: Nobody states the assumption, so it cannot be addressed, only worked around. There is no meeting at which it can be raised and resolved.
details.energy_note: An accusation nobody makes and everybody acts on.

details.aspect: The cumulative professional cost is large and invisible
details.description: Slower trust, fewer introductions, less sponsorship, more scrutiny of the same work. None of it appears in a performance review and all of it compounds over thirty years.
details.money_note: Lifetime earnings effect of slower trust and fewer sponsors.
details.energy_note: A career run at a slightly worse exchange rate.

issues.title: The marriage and relationship market, with the identity priced in
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
issues.summary: The user's brief names this directly and it is real: the identity changes who will partner with you, on what terms, and how the relationship is read by everyone around it - in both directions, at home and abroad.

details.aspect: Abroad, the identity is a filter applied by other people
details.description: Some partners and their families treat the nationality as a political complication, a security concern, or a visa liability, and withdraw on those grounds without ever naming them. The pattern is felt long before it can be articulated.
details.energy_note: Ended for reasons nobody will put in a sentence.

details.aspect: Being used and discarded is a specific, reported pattern
details.description: Relationships in which the Palestinian partner is a novelty, a political accessory or a cause rather than a person - intense, admiring, and ended when the cost of association becomes real. The brief names this and it belongs here: the harm is that the interest was never in you.
details.energy_note: Fascinating for a season, and then expensive.

details.aspect: At home, the document decides who is marriageable
details.description: The ID tiers convert marriage into an immigration calculation. A green ID marrying a blue ID means a family unification file; marrying a Gaza ID means separation. Families factor this in openly, and people are rejected for their paperwork.
details.energy_note: Turned down for the colour of your card.
details.notes: See FAM-001 and IDR-002 for the mechanism this is downstream of.

details.aspect: Unmarried women carry a specific stigma
details.description: Research on 'spinsterhood' in Palestine finds the societal expectation of marriage marginalises women who fall outside it, and that the number of unmarried women can become a locus of moral panic - in a society already under prolonged insecure and warlike conditions. The same work finds a long tradition of unmarried women leading full lives, which is the part that never gets quoted.
details.energy_note: A demographic statistic, experienced as a personal failing.

details.aspect: Widows and divorced women face a narrower market and lose custody either way
details.description: In Gaza, widows and divorced women historically had two options: marry a divorced or widowed man, or remain alone. Custody compounds it - when a divorced woman remarries her former husband tends to get the children; when a widow remarries her children tend to go to her late husband's family.
details.energy_note: Remarry and lose the children. Don't, and be alone.

details.aspect: Remarriage after martyrdom is sometimes about the children, not the widow
details.description: Norms shifted after the first intifada so that previously unmarried men may marry martyrs' widows - reportedly often less for the widow's welfare than to secure custody of her children.
details.energy_note: Proposed to, for your children.

details.aspect: The prisoner's wife is a category with no name and no end
details.description: Married to a man serving decades, she is neither married in practice nor free to remarry, running the household alone and the prison administration on top of it, indefinitely.
details.energy_note: Married to a visiting room.
details.notes: See FAM-003 and DET-004.

details.aspect: And the isolation removes the thing that buffers everything else
details.description: Partnership is the single largest protective factor against every stressor in this dataset. A market distorted by documents, politics and stigma removes it precisely from the people carrying the most.
details.energy_note: The main shock absorber, priced out of reach.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - custody as the mechanism, not a side effect
details.description: In Gaza, when a divorced woman remarries her former husband tends to get custody of the children; when a widow remarries, her children tend to be cared for by her late husband's family. Norms shifted after the first intifada so previously unmarried men may marry martyrs' widows - reportedly often to secure custody of the children rather than for the widow's welfare.
details.energy_note: Remarry, and the children go elsewhere.

issues.title: Learning to say nothing
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Where speech carries permit, employment, visa and naturalisation consequences, silence is the rational strategy - and practising it for years does specific damage.

details.aspect: The costs are documented, not imagined
details.description: A doxxing operation that states its purpose is to prevent employment, and tracks firings and deportations as metrics. A naturalisation clause requiring declarations. Permit decisions influenced by social media posts. The silence is a response to an accurate risk assessment.
details.energy_note: Not paranoia. Arithmetic.
details.notes: See DIA-001, STA-004, TEC-003.

details.aspect: It removes the ordinary processing mechanism
details.description: The normal response to a bad year is to describe it to people. That is exactly the behaviour that carries risk, so the processing does not happen and the material stays undigested.
details.energy_note: Nowhere safe to put any of it.

details.aspect: Self-censorship generalises beyond its original subject
details.description: Practised long enough, the caution stops being about one topic. People become guarded about their opinions generally, which reads as being closed, which costs them the relationships that would have helped.
details.energy_note: Careful about everything, eventually.

details.aspect: Academics self-censor their actual research
details.description: Where the subject is professionally dangerous, researchers choose other questions. The scholarship that would document all of this is thinner than it should be, for the same reason as everything else in this file.
details.energy_note: A literature with a hole in it, for cause.

issues.title: Threat that does not end, so there is no 'post'
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: Trauma frameworks assume the event has finished. Under an ongoing occupation the hypervigilance is an accurate reading of the present, which makes most of the treatment literature inapplicable.

details.aspect: The concept, and where it came from
details.description: Continuous traumatic stress was developed in the 1980s by clinicians in apartheid-era South Africa who found PTSD frameworks failed people whose victimisation was ongoing rather than finished.
details.energy_note: A diagnosis written for a war that ended.
details.notes: Fully developed in assets/text/war, PTS-002. Recorded here because it is the correct frame for this population specifically.

details.aspect: The symptoms are adaptive, which is why treating them fails
details.description: Avoiding a road during a closure and not sleeping during a raid are correct responses. Evidence: once a person leaves the affected area, symptoms subside dramatically - the opposite of what a conditioned false-alarm model predicts.
details.energy_note: Told to relax about something still happening.

details.aspect: It presents as rage and exhaustion rather than fear
details.description: The validated instrument loads on exhaustion/detachment, rage/betrayal and fear/helplessness - not PTSD's intrusion, avoidance and arousal. Clinicians looking for flashbacks miss it.
details.energy_note: It comes out as fury, and gets misread.

details.aspect: And there is no functioning system to treat it in
details.description: Mental health services are the first cut and the last restored, and the clinicians are living under the same conditions as the patients.
details.energy_note: Your therapist heard the same explosion.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the finding that safety is the treatment
details.description: The continuous-traumatic-stress literature reports that once a resident leaves the affected area, symptoms subside dramatically - the opposite of what a conditioned false-alarm model predicts, and the clearest evidence that the response is an accurate reading of the environment rather than a disorder.
details.energy_note: The symptoms stop when the shelling does.

issues.title: Waiting, as a permanent condition
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
issues.summary: Almost every hurdle in this dataset resolves into waiting for a decision by someone who owes no answer and keeps no deadline. Sustained uncertainty is a distinct injury from bad news.

details.aspect: Uncertainty does not habituate
details.description: A stress response adapts to a known bad outcome. It does not adapt to an unresolved one, because there is nothing to adapt to. This is why 'no answer' is harder than 'no'.
details.energy_note: The one state the mind cannot settle into.

details.aspect: It prevents both planning and acceptance
details.description: A refusal permits a new plan. A pending file permits neither continuing nor abandoning, so the person holds two incompatible futures open indefinitely.
details.energy_note: Can't move on, can't move forward.

details.aspect: Hope, kept at full strength, is the injury
details.description: The permit might come. The name might be on the next list. The bridge might reopen. Hope is functional and it is also what keeps the wound from closing.
details.energy_note: Hoping, continuously, as a form of damage.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the folder
details.description: It has her name, her mother's medical file, four rejected applications and one unanswered one. She has carried it to six offices. She knows exactly which page each of them will ask for.
details.energy_note: A life, in a plastic wallet, at a window.

issues.title: What it takes out of the work
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: The brief asks specifically for the effects on efficiency and growth. They are real, they are large, and they are attributed to the person rather than the conditions in essentially every setting.

details.aspect: Threat monitoring runs on the same budget as thinking
details.description: Sustained vigilance consumes the working memory and attention that would otherwise go to work and study. The capacity is finite and it is already committed.
details.energy_note: Concentration spent before the day starts.

details.aspect: Long-horizon projects stop being started
details.description: A business, a degree, a book, a house all require an assumption of continuity that is not available. The rational move is short-horizon, low-commitment activity - which is also the activity with no compounding returns.
details.energy_note: Never starting the thing that takes five years.

details.aspect: Administrative load is a second unpaid job
details.description: Permits, renewals, appeals, evidence files, embassy appointments, document legalisation. Days per year, every year, drawn from the same hours as the career.
details.time_note: Days per year on the administration of the hurdles in this file.
details.energy_note: A second job, unpaid, with no promotion.

details.aspect: Sleep is the first thing lost, and it is the input to everything
details.description: Night raids, sirens, blackouts, a phone that might ring, and the folder. Degraded sleep degrades judgement, mood, immune function and output, and it does so invisibly.
details.energy_note: Everything else, downstream of not sleeping.

details.aspect: It is scored as a character trait
details.description: Reduced output is appraised by employers, universities and even families as laziness, lack of ambition, or unreliability. The person receives the judgement, and frequently agrees with it.
details.energy_note: Judged for capacity that was already spent.

details.aspect: Which is the closing loop of this entire dataset
details.description: Conditions are imposed. The conditions reduce output. The reduced output is read as evidence about the person and the people. That evidence is then used to justify the conditions.
details.energy_note: The circle: made unable, then blamed for it.

issues.title: Back pain, and the fact that it is measured
issues.category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
issues.summary: The brief asks about back pain specifically. It is not a figure of speech: somatic symptom disorder has a published prevalence in Palestinian primary care, back pain is the second commonest presentation, and being female roughly doubles the odds.

details.aspect: The prevalence, and the symptom list
details.description: A cross-sectional study of 400 Palestinian primary health care attendees over 18 with no psychiatric diagnosis found somatic symptom disorder in 32.5% (95% CI 27.9-37.1). The commonest symptoms were painful muscles at 61.5% and back pain at 52.3%.
details.energy_note: A third of the waiting room, and half of them have back pain.

details.aspect: Being female roughly doubles it
details.description: Associations: female gender aOR 2.1, chronic disease 2.4, depression 3.3, anxiety 2.1, frequent primary care attendance 2.4.
details.energy_note: Twice the odds, for being a woman.

details.aspect: The authors name the context explicitly
details.description: The study notes somatisation increases use of existing services and the burden on staff, particularly in low- and middle-income countries like Palestine, 'which suffers from occupation and scarcity of resources'. The occupation is in the paper, not added by this dataset.
details.energy_note: The cause is named in the literature itself.

details.aspect: It produces years of the wrong investigations
details.description: The patient presents with back pain and receives imaging, then referral, then another opinion. Each is negative, each costs money and months, and each reinforces a sense of not being believed.
details.energy_note: Scanned repeatedly and told there's nothing wrong.

details.aspect: And 'it's stress' is heard as 'it isn't real'
details.description: A somatic diagnosis is routinely received as a dismissal. The pain is real, the mechanism is real, and the explanation lands as an accusation of fabrication.
details.energy_note: Told it's in your head, about a back that hurts.

details.aspect: Regionally it is the same picture
details.description: A review of somatic symptom disorders in the Arab world found muscle and back pain the most reported somatic symptoms, with comorbid depression, anxiety and trauma-related symptoms.
details.energy_note: The same two symptoms, across the region.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the study, and its own framing
details.description: 400 Palestinian primary care attendees over 18 with no psychiatric diagnosis: somatic symptom disorder in 32.5%, painful muscles 61.5%, back pain 52.3%, female gender aOR 2.1. The authors note somatisation increases service use and staff burden 'particularly in low- and medium-income countries like Palestine, which suffers from occupation and scarcity of resources'.
details.energy_note: The occupation is named in the paper, not added afterwards.

issues.title: Chronic pain, with the psychological load measured alongside it
issues.category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: A Gaza hospital study puts numbers on the combination the rest of this dataset describes: long-duration pain, near-universal psychological distress, and poverty, in the same patients.

details.aspect: The cohort
details.description: 272 Palestinian patients at Al-Shifa Hospital assessed with DASS-21 and pain catastrophising scales. Half were unemployed, 94.1% lived on under 1,974 ILS a month, and median pain duration was four years.
details.energy_note: Four years of pain, on under two thousand shekels a month.

details.aspect: The distress figures
details.description: Depression 83.1%, anxiety 83.8%, stress 88.6% - with pain catastrophising correlating strongly with psychological distress.
details.energy_note: Nearly nine in ten, on every measure.

details.aspect: The authors' recommendation is the one thing unavailable
details.description: They call for integrated, trauma-informed pain management addressing biomedical and psychosocial factors together - in a health system with 17 of 36 hospitals functioning.
details.energy_note: The right treatment, and nowhere to deliver it.

details.aspect: Pain of this duration reshapes a life, not a week
details.description: Four years median duration means work capacity, sleep, mood, parenting and relationships have all already reorganised around it before anyone measured anything.
details.energy_note: Long enough that it's just who you are now.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - 272 patients at Al-Shifa
details.description: Half unemployed, 94.1% living on under 1,974 ILS a month, median pain duration four years, depression 83.1%, anxiety 83.8%, stress 88.6%, with pain catastrophising correlating strongly with psychological distress.
details.energy_note: Four years of pain, and nearly nine in ten distressed.

issues.title: Stressful working conditions, and the back that carries them
issues.category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
issues.summary: The link between the conditions and the body has been measured in the occupational literature too, in the workforce that holds the health system together.

details.aspect: The nurses study
details.description: A cross-sectional study of Palestinian nurses found high perceived stressful working conditions adversely affect physical and mental health, and specifically found an association between back pain and self-reported stressful working conditions.
details.energy_note: The stress and the back pain, in the same regression.

details.aspect: Nursing here is a majority-female profession under siege conditions
details.description: The same workforce is the one being detained, killed and starved in ATR-001 and ATR-004. The occupational stress literature and the atrocity literature are describing the same people.
details.energy_note: The nurses in the stress study are the nurses in the detention reports.

details.aspect: The study design limits the causal claim and the direction is unsurprising
details.description: Cross-sectional data cannot establish causation, which the authors say. The association is consistent with everything else in this section.
details.energy_note: Association, not proof. Recorded as such.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the same workforce, two literatures
details.description: The Palestinian nurses in the occupational-stress study showing an association between back pain and stressful working conditions are drawn from the same profession documented in ATR-001 and ATR-004 as detained, tortured and killed in the hundreds.
details.energy_note: The stress study and the detention reports are about the same nurses.

issues.title: The productivity loss nobody has quantified
issues.category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: The brief asks about effects on efficiency and growth. The honest position is that the mechanism is well evidenced and the magnitude is not, because the study has not been done.

details.aspect: HONEST GAP - the absenteeism and output research does not exist
details.description: Searches of this literature surface somatic prevalence, chronic pain and occupational stress, but little quantifying workplace productivity loss or absenteeism in this population. It is an under-studied dimension, and this row says so rather than inventing a figure.
details.energy_note: The mechanism is documented. The number is not.

details.aspect: What can be said from the components
details.description: Somatic symptom disorder at 32.5% with back pain in half of those, chronic pain with 83-89% distress rates, degraded sleep, and 20-200 days a year of administrative load. Each has a known effect on output; nobody has multiplied them together for this population.
details.money_note: Order-of-magnitude only. Do not cite.
details.energy_note: Four large effects, never added up.

details.aspect: Why the study is not done is itself part of the dataset
details.description: Research requires funding, access, institutional stability and researchers willing to take the professional risk. EDU-001, PSY-003 and DIA-001 each remove one of those.
details.energy_note: The evidence gap has the same causes as the harm.

issues.title: Detaining the doctors and nurses
issues.category_name: Torture, deaths in custody and documented atrocities against civilians
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: Medical workers have been detained in numbers, held without charge for very long periods, and - according to multiple monitoring bodies - tortured. The interrogations reportedly concerned their hospitals and colleagues rather than any alleged offence.

details.aspect: The numbers detained
details.description: The Gaza Ministry of Health counted 310 health workers detained as of June 2024. Healthcare Workers Watch reported that by July 2025 over 400 Palestinian healthcare workers, including at least 28 doctors, had been detained since October 2023 - many held over 400 days without charge, and three for over 600 days.
details.energy_note: Four hundred days in custody, no charge, for being a nurse.

details.aspect: The proportion of one facility's population
details.description: Dr Khalid Hamouda, himself a detainee, estimated about a quarter of the roughly 100 detainees held at Sde Teiman were healthcare workers.
details.energy_note: One in four of the room, medical staff.

details.aspect: The PHRI findings
details.description: Physicians for Human Rights Israel published 'Unlawfully Detained, Tortured, and Starved: The Plight of Gaza's Medical Workers in Israeli Custody' in February 2025, based on testimony from 24 detainees - physicians, nurses and paramedics aged from at least 21 to 69 - visited by PHRI lawyers in military and prison service facilities after more than six months in isolation. It documented beatings, torture, psychological abuse, medical neglect and insufficient rations.
details.energy_note: Twenty-four testimonies, ages 21 to 69.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - specific methods, from the testimony
details.description: One detainee described being suspended by her wrists for hours. Others described being severely beaten under interrogation and subjected to prolonged high-volume music. Healthcare Workers Watch-Palestine collected 31 accounts describing stress positions, food and water deprivation, threats of sexual violence and degrading treatment.
details.energy_note: Suspended by the wrists, for hours.

details.aspect: The interrogations were about the hospital, not the person
details.description: Detainees were not charged or individually accused; interrogations focused on collecting information about their workplace, their colleagues and Gaza's health system. PHRI's Naji Abbas described this as aimed at finding information useful to the assault, and as a violation of Geneva Convention protections for medical workers.
details.energy_note: Held not for what you did, but for what you know about your ward.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - hospital directors taken with their staff
details.description: OHCHR gathered credible information that raids on hospitals often led to mass detention and enforced disappearance of medical staff, including the directors of Al Awda, Kamal Adwan, Al Shifa and Al Amal. Dr Muhammad Abu Salmiya, Al-Shifa's director, was held without charge for seven months until July 2024. Kamal Adwan's director Hussam Abu Safiya was detained along with more than 240 Palestinians including dozens of medical staff.
details.energy_note: The director, and two hundred and forty others.

details.aspect: The corroboration is unusually broad
details.description: HRW documented the same pattern in August 2024, as did B'Tselem in August 2024 and Healthcare Workers Watch. The IDF and Prison Service denied the allegations.
details.energy_note: Four bodies, the same finding, and a denial.

details.aspect: Removing the medical workforce is a harm to everyone else
details.description: Every detained surgeon is a queue that does not move, and every detained midwife is a birth without one. The harm to the population is separate from, and larger than, the harm to the detainee.
details.energy_note: The doctor is in prison, so the ward has no one.

issues.title: Dying in custody
issues.category_name: Torture, deaths in custody and documented atrocities against civilians
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: The Special Rapporteur on torture records deaths in custody in numbers, with a stated lack of transparency about causes. The most documented individual case is a surgeon who was never charged with anything.

details.aspect: The count
details.description: The Special Rapporteur on torture's May 2026 report notes 94 Palestinians died in custody from October 2023 through August 2025, acknowledging a lack of transparency about causes of death. A review of 10 postmortem examinations found signs of physical abuse in five of them.
details.energy_note: Ninety-four deaths, and half the autopsies reviewed show abuse.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - Dr Adnan al-Bursh
details.description: Head of orthopaedics at al-Shifa and a professor of orthopaedic medicine. Detained 19 December 2023 during an attack on Al-Awda Hospital in northern Gaza and taken to Sde Teiman. Fellow detainee Dr Khalid Hamouda said he was beaten for days, his ribs broken, until he could no longer walk unaided. Four months later he was transferred to Ofer Prison in the West Bank.
details.energy_note: A professor of orthopaedics, with broken ribs, unable to stand.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - and how it ended
details.description: Testimony collected by the Israeli rights group HaMoked describes him arriving at Ofer severely battered, naked from the waist down and unable to stand, thrown into the yard and left helpless. As a fellow prisoner helped him to a cell, screams were heard; minutes later prisoners were heard declaring him dead. The Palestinian Civil Affairs Committee said he died on 19 April, aged 50. His body remains withheld. Israel accused him of being a terrorist; like most detainees at Sde Teiman and Ofer he was never charged with any offence. The UN Special Rapporteur on the OPT expressed concern over his death, emphasising the likelihood of sexual violence as part of his torture.
details.energy_note: Fifty years old, never charged, body not returned.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - he was not the only one
details.description: Dr Iyad Al Rantisi also reportedly died in detention as a result of torture and ill-treatment. Dr Khaled Al Serr of the Nasser Medical Complex survived six months following the same route from Sde Teiman to Ofer, describing regular beatings including to intimate areas, and calling the treatment humiliating.
details.energy_note: A second doctor dead, a third who came back.

details.aspect: The body withheld is a second, continuing harm
details.description: Where remains are not returned there is no burial, no funeral, no grave and no point at which the death becomes a fact the family can act on. It converts a bereavement into an indefinite open state.
details.energy_note: No body, so no ending.
details.notes: Mechanism developed in assets/text/war, BER-001.

details.aspect: Scale of the detained population, for context
details.description: OHCHR figures cited in the 2026 Secretary-General's report indicate more than 9,000 Palestinians remain imprisoned, including over 4,000 in administrative detention. Israel continues to deny UN investigators access to detention facilities and to Gaza.
details.energy_note: Nine thousand held, and no inspector admitted.

issues.title: Sexual and gender-based violence in detention, found to be policy
issues.category_name: Torture, deaths in custody and documented atrocities against civilians
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
issues.summary: The UN Commission of Inquiry concluded that sexual, reproductive and other gender-based violence against Palestinian detainees was not incidental but an intentional policy forming part of standard operating procedures.

details.aspect: The March 2025 finding
details.description: The Commission concluded that mistreatment of Palestinian detainees resulted from an intentional policy of using sexual, reproductive and other forms of gender-based violence to humiliate and degrade Palestinians in detention, and that such practices increased significantly in severity and frequency after 7 October 2023.
details.energy_note: Not excesses. A policy, per the Commission.

details.aspect: What it found was standard procedure
details.description: Forced public stripping and nudity, sexual harassment including threats of rape, and sexual assault were found to de facto form part of standard operating procedures - and sexualised torture to have been committed with either explicit orders or implicit encouragement from top civilian and military leadership.
details.energy_note: Stripping, as a procedure rather than an incident.

details.aspect: The October 2024 report, on the legal characterisation
details.description: The Commission found thousands of child and adult detainees, many arbitrarily detained, subjected to widespread and systematic abuse amounting to the war crime and crime against humanity of torture, and the war crime of rape and other forms of sexual violence. It found both Israel and Palestinian armed groups responsible for torture and sexual and gender-based violence.
details.energy_note: Named as crimes against humanity, and not only on one side.

details.aspect: Impunity was treated as part of the finding
details.description: All documented incidents were met with impunity, which the Commission held makes civilian and military leaders as responsible as the direct perpetrators.
details.energy_note: Nobody punished, so everybody responsible.

details.aspect: It continued after the reports
details.description: The 2026 Secretary-General's report on conflict-related sexual violence stated that patterns of sexual violence against Palestinians in detention continued during 2025, and that verified cases should be understood as indicative of a broader pattern rather than an exhaustive list - particularly as Israel continues to deny UN investigators access.
details.energy_note: Documented, reported, and continuing.

details.aspect: Israel rejects the findings
details.description: Israel rejected the Commission's conclusions; the Prime Minister called the report biased and Israel's UN mission said IDF policies prohibit such misconduct. The dataset records the finding and the denial together.
details.energy_note: Findings, and the rejection of them, both on the record.

details.aspect: Disclosure afterwards carries its own cost for a woman
details.description: Where the community response to sexual violence is silence or blame, the released detainee has a second decision to make about whether to say what happened - and rational non-disclosure means the true prevalence is unknown and understated in every source including this one.
details.energy_note: A number nobody has, for reasons that are themselves the harm.
details.notes: Same mechanism as GNC-002 in assets/text/war.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the Commission's March 2025 conclusion, in its own terms
details.description: The UN Commission of Inquiry found forced public stripping and nudity, sexual harassment including threats of rape, and sexual assault de facto formed part of standard operating procedures, and that sexualised torture was committed with either explicit orders or implicit encouragement from top civilian and military leadership. Israel rejected the findings; the Prime Minister called the report biased and Israel's UN mission said IDF policies prohibit such misconduct.
details.energy_note: Found to be procedure, not excess - and formally denied.

issues.title: Attacking the health system itself
issues.category_name: Torture, deaths in custody and documented atrocities against civilians
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
