issues.summary: Beyond individual detentions, monitoring bodies record sustained attacks on hospitals, ambulances and health workers at a scale UN experts have described as 'medicide'.

details.aspect: The WHO attack count
details.description: WHO's Surveillance System for Attacks on Health Care recorded 735 attacks on health care in Gaza from 7 October 2023 to 11 June 2025, killing 917 people, injuring 1,411, affecting 125 health facilities and damaging 34 hospitals.
details.energy_note: Seven hundred and thirty-five attacks on health care.

details.aspect: Health workers killed
details.description: WHO has documented at least 1,580 health workers killed; the UN Human Rights Office reported at least 1,581, including doctors and nurses who died with their families in residential buildings and tents, and expressed grave concern about a pattern of intentional killings. The Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics reported at least 1,701 health sector workers killed between October 2023 and October 2025.
details.energy_note: Sixteen hundred doctors, nurses and paramedics.

details.aspect: The comparison that gives it scale
details.description: By mid-2024, health worker deaths in Gaza had already exceeded the combined total documented across all other global conflicts in 2022.
details.energy_note: More than every other war on earth, combined, in a year.

details.aspect: What is left running
details.description: B'Tselem reported only 17 of Gaza's 36 hospitals functioning and 2.5% of Gaza's medical personnel killed. WHO noted more than half of hospitals closed, with those still operating able to provide only very limited emergency, life-saving surgery and intensive care.
details.energy_note: Seventeen hospitals, for two million people.

details.aspect: The UN experts' characterisation
details.description: UN experts described the destruction of Gaza's healthcare system as 'medicide', stating that health and care workers have been 'continuously targeted, detained, tortured' and are now being starved along with the rest of the population.
details.energy_note: A word invented because the existing ones were too small.

details.aspect: Every row in the MED category depends on this one
details.description: The referral system, the permit queue and the specialty lottery in MED-001 to MED-004 all presuppose hospitals to be referred to. This issue is why those processes increasingly refer to nothing.
details.energy_note: A referral system pointing at rubble.

details.aspect: And it lands on women twice
details.description: Nursing and midwifery are majority-female professions here, so the workforce being killed and detained is disproportionately female - and the patients most dependent on the destroyed obstetric capacity are women. Both ends of WOM-006 run through this issue.
details.energy_note: The midwives are killed, and then there are no midwives.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the WHO surveillance count
details.description: 735 attacks on health care in Gaza between 7 October 2023 and 11 June 2025, killing 917 people, injuring 1,411, affecting 125 health facilities and damaging 34 hospitals. By mid-2024 health worker deaths in Gaza had already exceeded the combined total documented across all other global conflicts in 2022.
details.energy_note: More health workers than every other war on earth combined.
details.source_name: WHO Surveillance System for Attacks on Health Care

issues.title: Atrocities against civilians, and the problem of the record
issues.category_name: Torture, deaths in custody and documented atrocities against civilians
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
issues.summary: Beyond detention, monitoring bodies document killings, enforced disappearances and starvation as method. The specific hurdle recorded here is that the documentation is obstructed, so the record will always understate it.

details.aspect: Investigators are not admitted
details.description: Israel continues to deny UN investigators access to detention facilities and to Gaza. Every figure in this category is therefore a floor rather than an estimate.
details.energy_note: Every number here is the minimum.

details.aspect: Verified cases are explicitly described as indicative, not exhaustive
details.description: The 2026 Secretary-General's report states verified cases should be understood as indicative of a broader pattern rather than an exhaustive list. That caveat is doing a great deal of work.
details.energy_note: A sample, presented as a sample, read as a total.

details.aspect: Blackouts remove the ability to document from inside
details.description: Where connectivity is cut, events cannot be recorded, transmitted or verified at the time, and testimony gathered later is discounted precisely for being later.
details.energy_note: Unable to record it, then disbelieved for having no recording.
details.notes: See TEC-002.

details.aspect: Which produces a permanent evidentiary asymmetry
details.description: One party has full documentary capability and access to the territory; the other has neither. Any adjudication that weighs documented evidence will systematically favour the better-documented account.
details.energy_note: A trial where only one side was allowed a camera.

details.aspect: And for the individual, being disbelieved is its own injury
details.description: Survivors consistently describe official and social disbelief as harder than the events, because it converts an injury into a question about their honesty.
details.energy_note: Asked, politely, whether any of it happened.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the access refusal, stated by the UN
details.description: The 2026 Secretary-General's report on conflict-related sexual violence states that verified cases should be understood as indicative of a broader pattern rather than an exhaustive list, particularly as Israel continues denying UN investigators access to detention facilities and to Gaza.
details.energy_note: The UN saying, in its own report, that it was not allowed to count.

issues.title: At the moment of travel, the nationality does not exist
issues.category_name: Status, statelessness and a passport that is not a nationality
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: The brief asks for this specifically. It is not that the passport is weak - it is that in the systems that actually move people across borders, the country is frequently not an option that can be selected.

details.aspect: The code exists, and the label does not agree with itself
details.description: ISO 3166 assigns PS and PSE, listed as 'PS PALESTINE, STATE OF'. Older systems still carry 'PS Palestinian Territory, Occupied'. Depending on the implementation the entry files under P for Palestinian Territory, O for Occupied, or S for State of Palestine - so scanning a dropdown alphabetically frequently fails even where the entry is present.
details.energy_note: It's in the list. Under a letter you wouldn't think to check.

details.aspect: The document says a word that is not in the dropdown
details.description: Since 16 June 2023 the PA biometric passport's nationality field reads PALESTINIAN. The dropdown, where it exists, says 'Palestine' or 'Palestinian Territory'. The word on the document does not match the option on the form, and the traveller has to guess which mismatch is safer.
details.energy_note: The passport and the form disagree about what you are.

details.aspect: Some systems use codes that other systems reject outright
details.description: Some immigration authorities record nationality with three-letter codes that may be PSE, XXP, or other X-variants - the ICAO codes for unspecified or undefined nationality and for stateless persons. Booking systems that validate only against ISO 3166 reject those codes.
details.energy_note: Your nationality code is literally 'undefined'.

details.aspect: There is no home airline whose system is guaranteed to cope
details.description: Palestine has no operating national carrier, so there is no airline whose systems are built to handle these codes as routine, and foreign carriers' support agents are generally unfamiliar with the issue.
details.energy_note: No airline for whom you are a normal customer.

details.aspect: The mismatch surfaces later, at the worst point
details.description: Airline departure control transmits the MRZ code to border systems. A dropdown selection that differs from the MRZ can pass at booking and fail at check-in or at the border, by which time the flight is non-refundable.
details.energy_note: Fine at booking. Wrong at the gate.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the form with no answer
details.description: The visa portal requires country of birth. Her options are Israel, Jordan, and a blank. Her birth certificate says Gaza. She picks one, knowing that whichever she picks is a discrepancy against one of her other documents, and that the discrepancy is what they will ask about.
details.energy_note: Three options, none of them true.

details.aspect: The administrative erasure is felt as the political one
details.description: Being absent from a dropdown is trivial and is not experienced as trivial. It is the daily, mechanical form of the argument about whether the place exists, delivered by a web form, several times a year.
details.energy_note: Your country, not found, please select another.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the codes that mean 'undefined'
details.description: Some immigration authorities record Palestinian nationality with three-letter codes that may be PSE, XXP or other X-variants. The XX-prefixed codes are the ICAO codes for unspecified or undefined nationality and for stateless persons. A booking system validating only against ISO 3166 rejects them outright.
details.energy_note: The computer's word for you is 'unspecified'.

issues.title: Travelling on a document whose nationality field says 'Undefined'
issues.category_name: Status, statelessness and a passport that is not a nationality
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: East Jerusalem Palestinians mostly hold no passport at all. They travel on an Israeli laissez-passer that confers no nationality, states the holder's nationality as undefined, and carries a re-entry permit that can be forfeited.

details.aspect: What the document is
details.description: The Israeli laissez-passer, a red-covered travel document issued for two years by the Ministry of Interior to people who cannot obtain an Israeli passport - generally Arab residents of East Jerusalem and Druze permanent residents of the Golan. It is not a passport.
details.energy_note: A travel document, explicitly not a passport.

details.aspect: The nationality field
details.description: Holders are treated as permanent residents rather than citizens, and their nationality is listed as 'Undefined', 'Foreign', or 'Jordanian'. The document confers no nationality and permits travel only via Israeli airports.
details.energy_note: Nationality: Undefined. Printed, in your document.

details.aspect: The scale
details.description: Roughly 340,000 East Jerusalem Palestinians hold it - about 75% of all laissez-passer holders. Residents were offered citizenship after the 1967 annexation and most declined for political reasons.
details.energy_note: Three hundred and forty thousand people, no nationality.

details.aspect: The re-entry permit is the trap
details.description: Permanent residents have no automatic right of re-entry. The documents carry time-limited re-entry permits - three years for Jordan travel, one year via the airport - renewable only in person in Jerusalem. Failure to renew means forfeiting the right to return.
details.time_note: Per renewal, in person, in Jerusalem.
details.energy_note: Miss the renewal and you have lost your city.

details.aspect: Two documents, neither of which works alone
details.description: Most East Jerusalem Palestinians also hold Jordanian passports, but mostly temporary foreigner's passports rather than nationality passports, which cannot be used to transit Ben Gurion. A destination visa can be stamped in the Jordanian document while the Israeli one is used for exit and entry.
details.energy_note: Two documents, and you need both to make one journey.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the citizenship that exists only on paper
details.description: One traveller's document listed Jordanian citizenship while the holder had no actual Jordanian passport - and was therefore denied the Jordanian tourist visa needed to transit Amman. The classification is a holdover from the period of Jordanian rule in East Jerusalem.
details.energy_note: Refused a visa for being a citizen of somewhere you are not.

details.aspect: And some people cannot get any document from anyone
details.description: In some cases East Jerusalem applicants can obtain civil documents from neither Israel nor the Palestinian Authority. Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank cannot obtain PA travel documents without an Israeli-issued national number, which requires a record in the Israeli civil registry. Those without one are called Bidoon - without.
details.energy_note: Called 'without'. That is the word for the category.
details.notes: Closes the loop with IDR-001: the registry Israel controls is the precondition for any document at all.

details.aspect: Which is the whole dataset in one field on one form
details.description: A person exists, lives in a city her family has lived in for generations, and the space on her travel document where a nationality would go says Undefined. Everything else in these seven files is downstream of that.
details.energy_note: Undefined, and expected to prove otherwise at every window.
